💡 Key Takeaways
  • Boris Rosenfeld shows DW a photo of him with his daughter Sofia and can't hold back tears.
  • According to recent reports, helives in Israel, while Sofia is in Russia.
  • On October 7, a court in Moscow sentenced Rosenfeld to three and a half years in a penal colony.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Boris Rosenfeld shows DW a photo of him with his daughter Sofia and can't hold back tears. "This was the last time we saw her. Then she left for Moscow, and this whole case began," he states.

According to recent reports, helives in Israel, while Sofia is in Russia. For more than a month now, she has been behind bars on charges of financing extremism. The case goes back to two donations totaling 2,000 rubles (about $30) to the late opposition politician Alexei Navalny'sAnti-Corruption Foundation (FBK), which the Russian authorities have since designated as extremist.

On October 7, a court in Moscow sentenced Rosenfeld to three and a half years in a penal colony.

In a recent development, rosenfeld is a prominent ornithologist who has devoted her life to studying and protecting Arcticbirds. "Sofia was an avid young naturalist from childhood. She loved birds, horses and dogs," her father mentioned as he leafed through a photo album.

Sofia was a teenager when the family moved to Israel but she returned to Russia a few years later and now holds both Russian and Israeli citizenship.

In a recent development, she studied biology at Moscow State University and developed a significant scientific career in Russia. Her colleague, Alexandra Panyutina, who now also lives in Israel, explained that Rosenfeld was devoted to her work from an early age.

"Birds and the Arctic are the defining passions of her life," she said.

It has been revealed that rosenfeld was among the first Russian researchers to develop a systematic approach to monitoring migratory bird populations. To support her research, she even developed a special aircraft.

"They could fly at almost the same speed as the birds and observe them from a low altitude," states Dmitry (name changed), a colleague of Rosenfeld's. "It rapidly became clear that this was a unique method.".

It has been revealed that rosenfeld is considered to be one of the leading figures in Russian ornithology. Her work has extended well beyond Russia and she has been deeply involved in international research projects. In the field of migratory bird conservation, cross-border cooperation is essential.

Helmut Kruckenberg, the head of the German Institute for Wetlands and Waterbird Research (IWWR), said Rosenfeld was highly respected within the international scientific community.

According to recent reports, "She has done an enormous amount for nature conservation and for the protection of Siberian and Arctic species," he remarked. "What is happening to her is simply beyond comprehension for us.".

According to recent reports, in the summer of 2021, when Russian authorities designated Alexei Navalny's Anti-Corruption Foundation, also known as FBK, as an extremist organization, Rosenfeld was on a remote Arctic expedition without a phone or access to the internet. Therefore, she did not cancel her regular donations to the FBK immediately, doing so only after her return to the Russian capital Moscow.

Her friend Olga (name changed) described Sofia as a person of absolute honesty. According to her, Rosenfeld's donations to Navalny's foundation reflected a genuine desire to fight corruption. Through her work in Russia's regions, she had seen plenty of it firsthand.

"She was never involved in political activism. Her donations were solely intended to support anti-corruption work," noted her father Boris Rosenfeld. "It's unthinkable".

It has been revealed that for him and others close to her, the sentence came as a shock. Although prosecutors had requested a five-year prison term, friends and colleagues expected that she would receive a fine at most.

There were reasons for that expectation. According to calculations by independent media outlet Mediazona, about 85% of convictions in the 225 cases involving donations to Navalny's foundation have so far resulted in non-custodial sentences. Yet Rosenfeld got three and a half years in a penal colony.

Recent findings suggest that just a few months after Rosenfeld defended her doctoral dissertation in October 2025, her home was searched. She was also subject to travel restrictions. She continued to work but she had to cancel her annual summer expedition to the Arctic.

Even on the day of the sentencing, her conversations with  her colleagues focused largely on science:  "We discussed how the work could continue in Sofia's absence," Olga mentioned. "But no one really believed she would end up in prison.".

"The only thing we think about now is how to bring her here," Boris Rosenfeld says as he looks at the pictures from Sofia's last visit.

It has been revealed that friends and colleagues who spoke to DW say that his daughter never considered leaving Russia, even as the prospect of a prison sentence loomed. "Sofia would never have left. She simply can't imagine life without geese," says Dmitry.

In a recent development, now, her family, friends and colleagues are campaigning to have her sentence overturned. More than 1,000 people have signed an appeal to Russia's Presidential Council for Human Rights.

Boris Rosenfeld is also hoping for support from Israel but so far Israeli consular officials have not been granted access to his daughter in detention.

The two continue to write to each other and he is trying to keep his spirits high: "She writes that she's trying to adjust to life in prison, and that it's hard," he notes. "But she's a strong person.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leeds United could face a setback in their bid to sign Melvin Bard permanently, with the Nice loanee reportedly weighing his options amid concerns about a lack of regular first-team football at Elland Road.

The French defender has shown glimpses of his quality since arriving in Yorkshire, but limited opportunities under Daniel Farke could influence his decision when the current campaign ends.

According to a report from 90maat, Bard could turn down the chance to make his temporary spell at Leeds permanent if he cannot secure more playing time for the rest of the season.

The Whites can sign the 25-year-old for around £4.3 million next summer, with his versatility making him an attractive option for Farke’s defensive setup.

Bard can operate at left-back and as a left-sided centre-back, offering valuable depth across multiple positions. His performance against Tottenham Hotspur also demonstrated that he could make a meaningful contribution when given the opportunity.

However, Gabriel Gudmundsson remains the preferred option on the left, leaving the Frenchman with limited opportunities to establish himself in the starting lineup.

The former Lyon defender arrived at Leeds hoping to play an notable role, but his involvement has fallen short of expectations.

He has made just three Premier League appearances since joining the club, accumulating approximately 60 minutes of league football.

Gudmundsson’s impressive performances have made it difficult for Bard to break into Farke’s looks, while his brief appearance against Chelsea after impressing against Tottenham offered little encouragement.

Leeds could certainly benefit from retaining an experienced defender for a relatively modest transfer fee. However, Bard will also consider his long-term development when deciding his next move.

If his situation does not improve, the Frenchman could favour a club where he has a better chance of playing regularly rather than committing his future to Leeds.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Giovanni Malagò notes Italy’s players were behind his decision to bring Roberto Mancini back as coach, and believes the Azzurri can rebuild around their young talent.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, the FIGC commissioner and presidential candidate was speaking at a debate organised by La Stampa at the MAUTO museum in Turin.

According to recent reports, malagò took charge of Italian football after the national team failed to reach a third consecutive World Cup, beaten by Bosnia and Herzegovina in March. He then turned to Mancini, who had won Euro 2020 in his first spell in charge.

“A federation president has to listen to everyone, but then the moment comes when it’s my face on the line,” Malagò said. “There’s an unwritten rule that if you don’t go to the World Cup, you go home. If we go out against Bosnia, it means we’re not exactly phenomenal.

“There aren’t years to plan and programme. I chose Mancini because I know his ideas about young players, and I speak with the national team players, who tell me: ‘Mancini all the way.’”.

Italy’s Nations League campaign ended in disappointment. Despite beating France 3-1, the Azzurri lost 4-1 in Belgium and failed to progress. Malagò still sees reasons for optimism.

“We have to rebuild around young players. We had a great Nations League group. We lost to Belgium, but there’s light at the end of the tunnel,” he said.

“The senior team is only the peak of the movement, and Italy’s Under-21 side is very strong. We haven’t been to the Olympics with the Under-21s since 2008, and we’ve already laid all the right foundations to go back.”.

The FIGC presidential election takes place in just over two weeks, with Malagò facing former Milan executive Adriano Galliani.

  • Emile Heskey is standing in a warehouse, dressed in a black adidas tracksuit, trying to sell you a jar of curious sweet treats.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 07:00 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 07:35 EST, 26 November 2026.

Emile Heskey is standing in a warehouse, dressed in a black adidas tracksuit, trying to sell you a jar of curious sweet treats.

He smiles into the camera with the gentle-giant warmth that characterised his football career – but Heskey is in unfamiliar territory.

Behind him, stacked on shelf after shelf, are containers full of Supreme CBD gummies.

The man who scored in England's 5-1 thrashing of Germany in 2001, who scored 110 Premier League goals for Leicester, Liverpool, Birmingham, Wigan and Aston Villa plus seven more for his country, is, remarkably, trying to flog you an assortment of products containing cannabidiol, a legal but controversial ingredient derived from cannabis.

Today, he is promoting a tub of CBD strawberry gummies, as well as oil. If you fancy an exclusive discount, there's a special code bearing his name.

‘I swear by these products for my sleep,’ he writes in the caption on Instagram. ‘They have been fantastic for me for years now!’.

Emile Heskey spends his days trying to flog controversial Supreme CBD products (Instagram: theemileheskey).

He is one of multiple former footballers promoting the products for ex-Olympic boxer Anthony Fowler - despite their illegal claims about the supposed health benefits.

According to recent reports, heskey, 48, was once one of English football's most respected players. He won 62 caps for England, appearing at two World Cups. He won five trophies at Liverpool and two League Cups at Leicester.

Recent findings suggest that occasionally mocked for his lack of goals – he averaged roughly one every five games during his club career – he carried himself with humour and grace. Since retiring, his reputation has helped him secure roles with England's youth pathway and Leicester's women's team, as well as occasional punditry work for the BBC.

According to recent reports, in September, he scored in an England legends match against Poland, playing alongside John Terry and Robbie Fowler. This month, he was a guest of honour at Liverpool's Anfield VIP Experience. He remains a regular on the speakers' circuit, with more appearances booked before Christmas.

All of which begs the question: what is he doing promoting Supreme CBD? Why is he filming several videos a month for a company with such a troubled regulatory record?

Where once he shared a dressing room with Steven Gerrard and David Beckham, he now shares an ambassadorial roster with Katie Price.

It is unclear whether Heskey is aware of the concerns surrounding Supreme CBD products, or the repeated occasions on which the company has fallen foul of advertising rules.

Its founder, Anthony Fowler, a former Team GB Olympic boxer, has made unsubstantiated claims that his cannabidiol products can help treat mental health conditions and autism in children.

There is likely a financial incentive for Heskey, although the terms of any arrangement are unclear. Equally, he appears genuinely convinced of the products' benefits. He claims the oil has done wonders for his sleep and eased his aches and pains.

Heskey's wife Chantelle has issued divorce proceedings - and claims he cancelled a holiday with their kids to go away with his upcoming partner instead.

Heskey and his new partner Jade Slusarczyk spent two weeks together in Cyprus and Greece.

Chantelle branded Heskey 'vile' and claimed he deleted her comment on an Instagram post about the latest couple's holiday.

Recent findings suggest that that may well be true. The NHS acknowledges that CBD has some medical uses, but warns that the ‘quality and content’ of products sold online can be uncertain and that they ‘may be illegal and potentially dangerous’. Nor is there any guarantee that products sold in health stores will be of ‘good quality’.

Recent findings suggest that supreme CBD have repeatedly breached advertising rules. In June, the Advertising Standards Authority took action over the manufacturer's continued use of prohibited claims that CBD could treat, prevent or cure human disease.

The regulator has also upheld complaints about celebrity promotions that failed to make clear they were advertisements.

Industry observers note that supreme CBD have made claims that their products can treat anxiety, insomnia and depression. Such medicinal claims are prohibited in advertising for products that have not been authorised as medicines. It is uncomfortable ground for Heskey to find himself on.

Sources indicate that last year, Fowler also spoke about refusing chemotherapy for his two-year-old daughter's tumour, claiming CBD oil had had a 'massive' effect on it instead. Price, a paid brand ambassador, amplified those claims on her own social media channels, including posted to her 1.6million followers on X that the tumour had 'shrunk' as a result.

British medical and food safety authorities advise that CBD should not be given to those under the age of 18.

In a recent development, CBD can also affect how other medicines work, meaning anyone using it alongside other treatments should seek medical advice. Certain medicinal CBD treatments require regular monitoring because of their potential effects on the liver.

It is not unusual for former sportspeople to struggle with insomnia, depression or persistent pain after retirement. In a digital world where anyone can extol the virtues of a product to thousands of followers, it is perhaps unsurprising that cannabis oil has attracted so much attention. Some consumers say it has helped them.

Heskey celebrates with David Beckham after scoring for England against Denmark at the 2002 World Cup.

Many of Heskey's almost 100,000 Instagram followers appear equally enthusiastic, with comments beneath his posts endorsing the benefits he describes.

Industry observers note that and Heskey is hardly alone among former footballers. Supreme CBD products have also been endorsed by former Arsenal and England playmaker Paul Merson – who has his name on a bundle of his 'favourite' products available to buy on the manufacturer's website – Heskey's old Liverpool team-mate Chris Kirkland, Southampton hero Matt Le Tissier and ex-Nottingham Forest goalkeeper Mark Crossley, while ex-Liverpool striker John Aldridge has insisted the product was ‘good for me’.

Life after football has, at times, been rather messy for Heskey.

In 2009, his wealth was estimated at £12million. He had built a clean-cut image and maintained a relatively low profile away from the pitch. Yet just a year later, in 2010, he was declared bankrupt.

Sources indicate that his subsequent business dealings have brought further difficulties. Earlier this year, Heskey became caught up in a legal dispute surrounding an allegedly fraudulent £15m takeover of Cypriot club Apollon Limassol by British businessman Craig Gabriel.

According to recent reports, heskey had been lined up to become the face of the takeover and a club director. There is no suggestion of wrongdoing on his part.

In 2023, Heskey was found to have defaulted on £92,000 in tax relating to his work as a football development officer between 2017 and 2020. He was handed a £42,000 penalty.

That same year, a celebrity bar and restaurant he had funded, and which was overseen by his wife Chantelle, was wound up by the courts with debts totalling £163,000.

Former England footballer Heskey has found love with former Miss Blackpool Slusarczyk.

Sources indicate that parea, which opened in 2018, had been a regular haunt of footballers and television personalities, including members of the Real Housewives of Cheshire cast. But a local catering tech giant applied to have the business wound up over unpaid debts.

The restaurant had previously made headlines in 2019 when its first anniversary party featured sushi served on a semi-naked woman lying on a table, her modesty largely preserved by strategically placed leaves and pieces of salmon.

In 2024, Heskey faced further financial difficulties linked to his involvement in a celebrity investment scheme that became embroiled in a £1.6billion tax dispute.

Recent findings suggest that the scheme was reportedly operated by Ingenious Media, a financing company that backed dozens of films. Investors were mentioned to include Beckham, Gerrard, Jeremy Paxman, Robbie Williams and Heskey, with a minimum investment of £50,000.

Gerrard and the composer Andrew Lloyd Webber were among those who launched legal proceedings against HSBC in 2018, alleging that the bank had ‘dishonestly assisted’ Ingenious Media.

In the same year, Heskey was ordered to pay almost £200,000 in a dispute involving an unpaid £1.63m tax bill.

His personal life has also become complicated. Heskey appears to be estranged from his wife Chantelle, whom he married in 2014 and with whom he has four children. In August, she branded him ‘vile’ following a holiday he took with his fresh partner.

Heskey had gone public with his relationship with Jade Slusarczyk, a former Sky Sports walk-on girl accompanying darts players to the oche, in July. Within a month, the couple were holidaying in Cyprus and Greece, sharing photographs of their trip on Instagram.

Parea, a popular Cheshire bar loved by footballers and celebrities and owned by Heskey and his wife, was wound up with debts of £163,000.

Industry observers note that ‘The best two weeks away with you,’ he wrote. The posts provoked an angry response from Chantelle, who has begun divorce proceedings and accused Heskey of letting his family down in comments beneath the photographs. She subsequently claimed that Heskey had deleted her comment and described him as ‘vile’.

Daily Mail Sport has contacted Mrs Heskey's representatives on multiple occasions, but they have declined to comment.

Recent findings suggest that emile and Chantelle have two sons, Reigan and Jaden, both footballers, and two younger daughters, Milanna and Mendez. Jaden made his Manchester City debut in the Carabao Cup last season and is now on loan at Sheffield Wednesday, while Reigan was sold to Cologne in the summer.

According to recent reports, speaking to Daily Mail Sport last year, Heskey praised his sons' athletic ability and suggested that both could one day play for England's senior team. He was happy to talk on that occasion, speaking as he helped coach children at a football camp.

Recent findings suggest that this time, however, Daily Mail Sport has been met with silence. We have made repeated attempts, through multiple reporters, to put questions to Heskey about his involvement with Supreme CBD. His representatives have either declined to comment or failed to respond.

It has been revealed that we wanted to know whether he was aware of the advertising rulings against Supreme CBD, and whether he had any concerns about the medical claims made by its founder. We would also have welcomed his account of the personal and financial difficulties described here.

But those questions remain unanswered.

And so we are left watching Heskey from afar, returning to the warehouse for video after video, smiling and cracking jokes with Fowler.

Heskey scores the fifth goal in England's 5-1 trouncing of Germany in 2001.

We have made repeated attempts to put questions to Heskey about his involvement with Supreme CBD. His representatives have either declined to comment or failed to respond.

‘When you find the best dose for you, there's no going back,’ he declares in the caption to one post from October.

Perched on a green sofa, encouraging his followers to buy products from a firm with a deeply controversial advertising record, he seems entirely at ease.

Whether Heskey has any reservations about the business whose products he so enthusiastically promotes is something we would dearly like to know.

For now, the former England striker is still smiling for the camera.

Falk suggested Bayern had been prepared to offer around €70 million (£58.5m) for Ngumoha during the summer, but Liverpool rejected their approach. The German side had hoped another opportunity could emerge, potentially with the youngster approaching the final year of his contract.

However, his recent performances have made that scenario less likely, leaving Bayern potentially needing to explore alternative targets.

Scherhant could therefore be a more realistic option for the Bundesliga champions as they look to reinforce their attack without pursuing an increasingly difficult deal for Ngumoha.

Adriano Galliani has hit back at Giovanni Malagò, claiming Juventus, Inter and Milan are among the Serie A clubs who have switched sides in the race for the FIGC presidency.

With quotes via La Gazzetta dello Sport, the two candidates traded light-hearted jabs on Thursday, with the election now just over two weeks away.

It has been revealed that speaking on the sidelines of a CONI council meeting, Malagò suggested he wouldn’t have run in Galliani’s position. He pointed to the U-turn made by the “technical components”, meaning the players’ union (AIC) and the coaches’ association (AIAC).

“What would I have done in Galliani’s place? Honestly, I wouldn’t have stood, given the U-turn by the technical components,” Malagò said. “But Adriano is a friend, and I’ll never say anything that isn’t affectionate. So I say it with a smile, even if I think this view is widely shared.”.

Asked whether Galliani was mounting a late comeback, Malagò added: “I’ve never been chasing in this game. It’s an electoral contest like many I’ve fought, even if there have been some strange positions.”.

Galliani, the former Milan and Monza executive, had his reply ready when he was approached leaving the PalaEur. He had been there for Italy’s basketball game against Turkey, which Malagò also attended.

“To my friend Giovanni, I’d say I stood because, as well as the technical components, a U-turn was also made by eight or nine Serie A clubs, including big ones like Juventus, Inter and Milan,” he said with a smile.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the report spans more than 150 pages, but its conclusion can be summed up in a single sentence: "The global situation regarding freedom of religion and belief deteriorated during the reporting period," stated Thomas Rachel, the German government's commissioner for freedom of religion and belief, and a member of parliament for the center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU). Recently adopted by the Cabinet, the government's fourth report on the subject covers developments from 2023 to 2025.

Recent findings suggest that the government has issued a dedicated report on freedom of religion and belief around the world. According to the report, this freedom is facing "increasing pressure" globally. The focus is not primarily on the suppression of religious institutions or structures, but on the situation of individuals who hold a religious belief, or none at all.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that the importance of religious freedom is reflected in the way the government commissioner describes the glitch: "Religion and faith are of great importance to four out of five people around the world and are central to their identity. People wake up with God and go to sleep with God. It is part of their everyday lives." Research by the Pew Research Center suggests that about 84% of the world's population identifies with a certain religion.

At a time when authoritarian regimes are gaining ground and expanding their surveillance capabilities, the report paints a bleak picture. The growing number of violent conflicts, the rise of authoritarian rule, and the spread of populism have led to "painful restrictions on freedom of religion and belief around the world.".

The German government report does not attempt to provide a statistical tally of attacks or the number of people facing persecution. Instead, it examines 30 countries as case studies where, in the federal government's view, freedom of religion and belief is being restricted. These include about six countries each from Africa, Asia, and the Arab world. In Europe, the report focuses on Belarus, Russia, Ukraine, and Turkey, while in Latin America it highlights Mexico, Nicaragua, and Cuba. It also identifies shortcomings in five of the world's six most populous countries: China, India, Indonesia, Pakistan, and Nigeria.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Regarding India, the report refers to "Hindu nationalist efforts" that threaten the equal treatment of all officially recognized religions. It states that the generally peaceful coexistence of different faiths is "repeatedly overshadowed by tensions and, at times, violence." Both Muslim and Christian communities report growing intolerance and hate speech. According to the report, violent Hindu extremist groups have carried out a "large number of physical attacks" against Muslims, while the police and government authorities often respond inadequately.

In China, the German government identifies a "significant tightening of the legal framework of state control at the expense of freedom of religion and belief." According to the report, this particularly affects Uyghurs, Tibetans and churches that lack official state approval and are subject to harsh measures by the authorities. The law on the "Promotion of Ethnic Unity and Progress," which came into force on July 1, 2026, subordinates religion to "the formation of national identity" and patriotic education.

One of the countries where the situation has deteriorated most dramatically is Nicaragua, which has severely restricted freedom of religion and belief since 2018. The repression has primarily targeted the Catholic Church. According to the report, "intimidation, persecution, imprisonment, and expulsion" have forced around 130 priests and nuns to leave the country.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The reports reserves some of its sharpest criticism for Kirill, the patriarch of the Russian Orthodox Church. Under his leadership, the church has strongly supported Russia's war against Ukraine and portrayed it as a "holy war." According to the report, "weapons are blessed, Russian soldiers are absolved of their sins, and donations are collected for the war." It is perhaps the clearest example in the report of how religion can be used to justify oppression and violence.

In a recent development, the report explicitly addresses the threat posed by "transnational repression" (TNR), which it describes as a "growing global problem" that also affects Germany. The term refers to the persecution or intimidation of individuals by their country of origin beyond its own borders.

Ultimately, it argues, this amounts to a "continuation of domestic repression." Such "cross-border repression" has become considerably easier through the growing availability of digital means of repression, including smear campaigns on social media and spyware.

According to recent reports, these forms of pressure range from physical attacks on individuals to digital assaults such as online intimidation and defamation. In some cases, repression is also carried out by threatening family members who remain in the country of origin. Russia and Iran, for example, are identified as the "main perpetrators of transnational repression" in Germany.

China is a particularly prominent example of religious and ideological tensions. Repression by Beijing in Germany primarily targets members of groups that the country's Communist Party classifies as "hostile to the system." These include Uyghurs, Tibetans, and members of the Falun Gong movement. According to the report, they are "also subject to surveillance and repressive measures in Germany," while relatives living in China are pressured.

Thomas Rachel hopes the newly published report will be "discussed in as many Bundestag committees as possible" and that members of parliament will "engage with the issue accordingly." Previous government reports on the subject have been debated in the Bundestag plenary at least once and, in some cases, twice.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The issue's place within the German government has also changed during the current legislative term. Commissioner Thomas Rachel is now based at the Foreign Ministry, while both of his predecessors since 2018 were attached to the Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development. Today, Rachel states, the importance of religion is being "taken into account" in German foreign policy. He also points to his involvement in the Foreign Ministry's diplomatic training programs.

According to recent reports, in doing so, the government led by Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) reversed a structural decision made by the previous center-left coalition, which was led from 2021 to 2025 by Chancellor Olaf Scholz of the Social Democratic Party (SPD). The Scholz government had reduced the glitch's prominence by assigning it to the "Religion and Foreign Policy" division. Religion and foreign policy have now regained a more prominent place within government.

It has been revealed that one example is the current foreign minister, Johann Wadephul, who has already visited the Vatican more often than his two predecessors combined. In addition, alongside Rachel, the ministry has for some time maintained a dedicated unit headed by an ambassador that deals with, among other things, "fundamental concerns relating to religion and foreign policy.".

The pressure is building on Palace head coach Pierre Sage, who desperately needs a win to lift the mood and propel the club out of the relegation zone. Nottingham Forest’s impressive 3-1 win over Manchester City on Saturday evening means that Palace have dropped to a lowly 19th and are two points from safety. To make matters worse, Sage’s beleaguered side have also conceded the most goals in the division (21 in nine games).

Meanwhile, Liverpool also endured midweek European torment, as Andoni Iraola’s men fell to an error-ridden 3-2 defeat away at Fenerbahce in the Champions League, having previously lost 1-0 to Arsenal in their most recent Premier League encounter on Merseyside last weekend, which has left the club in sixth but just five points behind second-place Man City.

Speaking to reporters on Friday, Iraola noted: “I think that’s the challenge, especially in a club like Liverpool. One week ago in this same press conference, we were on a run, everything was in a good place and we were in a better mood. And now, two defeats, it changes. It has to change and it has to be like this in a club like ours. Now we have to react after two defeats.”.

According to recent reports, as for Palace’s team news, Jean-Philippe Mateta is serving the first match of a three-game domestic ban after he was sent off for Palace in the 2-0 defeat to Tottenham last time out in the league. Nottingham Forest's restless players have already seen off two managers in the past 12 months but now Oliver Glasner believes he will beat them at their own game.

The strength of feeling within the squad helped force Ange Postecoglou and Sean Dyche out of the door after 39 and 114 days respectively and after a dodgy start to his reign, there were probably one or two who thought Glasner would go the same way.

Recent findings suggest that no Premier League boss is ever immune to results and another run of defeats would make Glasner vulnerable. Forest have won two games all season and are above the relegation zone only on goal difference, ahead of Friday night’s clash with Chelsea at the City Ground.

But as things stand, Glasner has the backing of Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis to make the changes he needs – and that could be bad news for some senior players.

Daily Mail Sport examines the power struggle bubbling away at the City Ground...

Nottingham Forest's restless players have already seen off two managers in the past 12 months but now Oliver Glasner believes he will beat them at their own game.

Glasner took aim at some players' lack of English skills in light of a disappointing start to the season that sees his side hovering outside the relegation zone on goal difference alone.

Early in his reign, Mikel Arteta stamped his authority on Arsenal, moving on high-profile players like Mesut Ozil, Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang and Alexandre Lacazette.

In a recent development, even at the start of his managerial career, Arteta would not compromise and was prepared to clash with big names if they would not match his standards. Arteta knew what he wanted and if he had to fight some stars to get it, all well and good. Now look where Arsenal are today.

Sources indicate that it will not have escaped Glasner that despite their success, the champions work ferociously hard and seem to carry no outsized egos or sense of entitlement. That may worry certain Forest players.

This is the source of Glasner’s remarks about players not learning English – but that is not his only issue with the squad. He wants time-keeping to be sharper, training sessions to be slicker.

It is thought Forest will listen to offers for Ola Aina and Callum Hudson-Odoi in January, while Ibrahim Sangare has work to do to force his way into Glasner’s prepares. Hudson-Odoi and Aina are influential figures in the dressing room and Sangare is highly respected, too. Is Glasner trying to smash this power base in order to cement his own?

Sources indicate that glasner wants to add more athleticism and physicality to his squad in January as he has been alarmed at how Forest have been outmuscled in certain games. As things stand, he has the mandate to shape things his way after a three-hour meeting with Marinakis in London this week.

In a recent development, it will not be easy. Glasner can change some things yet a fair number of this squad are on their fifth manager. They were outstanding for a season under Nuno Espirito Santo in 2024-25 but they have drifted since. It still feels a long way until January and that is why – more than ever – Glasner needs the captain on board...

Glasner wants players' time-keeping to be sharper and training sessions to be slicker.

It is thought Forest will listen to offers for influential full back Ola Aina in January.

A glance at the numbers shows that Morgan Gibbs-White is having an outstanding season. He has created the second-most big chances of any player, the third-most chances from open play, and is in the top three for 'expected assists' too. Not bad for a player in a team above the relegation zone thanks only to goal difference.

Albeit from a smaller sample size, Gibbs-White is performing better than last term on all of these metrics (per 90 minutes). Last season, he finished with 15 league goals and four assists. England boss Thomas Tuchel appreciates the underlying numbers and after leaving Gibbs-White out of his World Cup squad, has brought him back into the fold this autumn.

Gibbs-White is Forest’s most talented player and it is believed he would have accepted a move away from the club last summer, after watching Elliot Anderson join Manchester City.

Sources indicate that there was tentative interest from Chelsea but Gibbs-White wanted to play in the Champions League and it is thought he would have been open to a move to Manchester United. The 26-year-old’s boyhood idol was Wayne Rooney – but the Old Trafford club have never truly pushed for him. That may change if Bruno Fernandes leaves next summer.

Recent findings suggest that gibbs-White is the highest-paid player in Forest's history and is halfway through a three-year deal. Few expect him to be at the club for life and if he moves in summer 2027, nobody will be surprised.

Sources indicate that yet there is a feeling in the game that Gibbs-White’s body language can count against him at times. When team-mates are not quite on his wavelength, Gibbs-White is often quick to show his frustration. If he creates a chance that a colleague misses, it is a similar story.

Morgan Gibbs-White's numbers are very impressive this season. At times, the same can't be said for his body language.

It is difficult to be rational in the heat of battle but could Gibbs-White try to stop these issues at source? At Forest, each part of the team – defenders, midfielders and forwards – have discussions before matches. That would be the perfect opportunity for Gibbs-White to guide others, to explain his thinking and where they should be when he has the ball in certain areas.

In a recent development, because unless the player is Diego Maradona or Lionel Messi, top clubs do not look at talent alone before making signings. Gibbs-White has the tools to play for an elite team but in other aspects, there may still be some work to do.

It has been revealed that glasner and his staff hope Forest’s best player can inspire others, as he has in the past. Club skipper Ryan Yates returned to the starting XI for the last two matches and if he loses his place against Chelsea, Gibbs-White would logically regain the armband. How Forest need a captain’s performance from him against Xabi Alonso’s faltering side.

Moscow, meanwhile, confirmed a further strike on Friday night in Kryvyi Rih.

Russia's Defense Ministry stated a thermal power plant in the city was hit, along with a power substation in the region of Rivne, on the opposite side of the country.

Both facilities supply electricity to the industry supporting Ukraine's military, the ministry added.

Elsewhere in the nearly five-year-long war, Russia ​also struck a ​cargo vessel ‌near Odesa, which Moscow mentioned was carrying dual-use goods ​for ⁠the Ukrainian military.

Eleven people, including two children, were wounded when a Russian drone attacked a five-story apartment building in the northeastern Kharkiv region, Ukraine’s State Emergency Service mentioned Saturday.

One person was wounded in a Russian attack on the capital, Kyiv, according to the service.

In Russia, local officials stated Saturday that Ukrainian drone attacks wounded three people in the Bryansk and Belgorod border regions.

Finland, meanwhile, stated it detected a drone attack on Saturday morning on a Russian cargo ship in the eastern Baltic Sea, prompting Prime Minister Petteri Orpo to warn that the war is "spilling over into our immediate vicinity.".

After damage to Russia's Kerch bridge to Crimea, Zelenskyy warned in an interview with US broadcaster NBC that the structure "will not remain standing anyway.".

Arsenal's greatest strength at the moment is their defensive solidity, with the physical prowess and technical quality within their backline making them the best in Europe.

His form has tailed off since then, and he has three goals and one assist in nine league appearances.

The injury could also affect his future. Sassuolo paid €500,000 to take him on loan in the summer and included an option to buy fixed at €12m, while Juventus kept a buy-back clause. A long spell out leaves both clubs with little to go on when they decide his future next summer.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Among other things, he is suggesting a tax on massive tech firms to ease the contributions of member states, some of which strongly criticised earlier proposals.
  • The EU budget is theEuropean Union’s shared budget and it is used for things ranging from agricultural subsidies, infrastructure projects to border control and defence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

European Council President Antonio Costa has proposed a newly introduced draft for the next EU budget.

Among other things, he is suggesting a tax on massive tech firms to ease the contributions of member states, some of which strongly criticised earlier proposals.

The EU budget is theEuropean Union’s shared budget and it is used for things ranging from agricultural subsidies, infrastructure projects to border control and defence.

A first draft for the 2028 to 2034 budget was proposed by the EU Commission in 2025 but was criticised, especially by a group of northern European members including Germany who wanted the budget to be much smaller.

Following that criticism, the European Council President has now suggested a latest draft, which is smaller by €204 billion.

But divisions among member states appear to remain, with France immediately coming out against Costa’s upcoming draft, saying it was "deeply disappointing.".

The proposal includes a string of latest "revenue channels," explicitly intended to "to keep national contributions at a reasonable level," so that member state will have to contribute less than otherwise would be the case.

The biggest splash would likely come from a tax on companies with an annual turnover from digital activities of at least 50 million euros in the EU and 750 million euros worldwide.

Those firms would be subject to "an annual contribution corresponding to 3% of the annual net turnover from online advertising, digital intermediation services and user-generated data," according to Costa.

Aside from the tech tax, the "balanced basket of fresh own resources" also includes taxes on tobacco products and electronic waste.

According to recent reports, neither the EU Commission nor European Council President Costa will have the final word on the budget. Costa's strategy will now be at the centre of hours of talks when EU leaders meet in Brussels next week.

Industry observers note that "This is a realistic budget that addresses our upcoming priorities while preserving our established policies," Costa wrote about his proposal. "I am confident that this proposal is a good basis for moving towards a final agreement.".

But an initial reaction from France suggests that any final agreement might still be some way off.

The French presidency mentioned the budget "falls well short ​of ‌what is needed, particularly on ‌the Common Agricultural Policy, ‌notably ​to guarantee income support for farmers.".

"As it ⁠stands, ​this proposal ​from the President ​of the European ‌Council does not ​provide ⁠a basis for an ⁠agreement.".

The EU was hoping to reach a general agreement on the budget by the end of 2026 with its formal adoption planned for 2027.

Even when the team won the Premier League title two seasons ago, there was a never-ending subplot about the futures of Mohamed Salah, Virgil van Dijk and Trent Alexander-Arnold.

Now there is ambiguity over Van Dijk again, plus Alisson, Alexis Mac Allister and others, with the depth of Liverpool's squad still an problem to be addressed.

But they broke this rule two years ago to offer Van Dijk a newly introduced deal. Will they do it again?

Liverpool's owners FSG broke their rule on offering 30-somethings big deals two years ago to tie down Virgil van Dijk. They should do it again.

Van Dijk is yet to be offered a new deal at Liverpool but this is not a reason for fans to panic. They always bide their time with these things.

Liverpool are carefully managing Van Dijk’s workload for the first time, as evidenced by him being a substitute in Bruges this week. The squad have had a day off on Thursday ahead of returning to training on Friday for the Merseyside derby.

Our verdict: There is a narrative that Van Dijk is starting to show his age. Maybe he is not quite at the extraordinarily high level he maintained in previous years but the skipper is still integral to everything the Reds do. If the two parties can agree on a one-year extension, it would suit everyone. But the Reds must also prepare for life without the formidable Dutchman, whenever that actually happens.

But there are still 18 months until his deal expires. What if his form falls off a cliff again as it did last season? No one was desperate for a new deal then. Liverpool should bide their time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Talk about cramming everything in. Brian Brobbey only played for 67 minutes but, in that time, he collected a yellow card, ripped Levi Colwill’s shirt and earned himself a standing ovation after morphing into a battering ram.

Sources indicate that régis Le Bris, Sunderland’s head coach, said there was nobody like the Netherlands striker in the Premier League and it said everything that everyone wanted to make Brobbey centre of attention after a long overdue home win, even though he had not scored. Everyone, that is, bar Xabi Alonso.

“No, he’s not unstoppable,” Chelsea’s head coach replied when asked why his team had found Brobbey too much to handle. “He’s stoppable – but only when you defend better than we did. We were not bullied. We didn’t produce enough.”.

That is one way of putting it. Another would be to say Brobbey was everything that Chelsea, much to Alonso’s disgust, were not: a bristling menace, a steamroller wearing a pair of boots, a player on a mission to help transform the mood – Enzo Le Fée’s decisive spot kick owed everything to Brobbey.

Chelsea arrived on Wearside looking to establish themselves in the top four ahead of the break but, instead, Alonso watched through his fingers as Sunderland reminded everyone why they were the joyous story of last season, a beautiful mix of inspiration and perspiration.

In fairness to the Chelsea manager, he refused to get caught in the minutiae of contentious penalty decisions – one that Chelsea were denied, another that they conceded – and could only lament as Sunderland ground out their first Premier League win since August 30, 70 long days ago.

Recent findings suggest that “It wasn’t the best game,” Alonso said. “I think that we didn’t deserve more than probably one point, maybe. We need to be more consistent on the move, to get the ball from one side to the other, and we didn’t do that good enough. We didn’t produce enough to deserve to win.”.

It has been revealed that unlike Sunderland. If you had turned up at the Stadium of Light without looking at the Premier League table, you would not have believed the hosts were bottom and you would not have given credence to the idea Le Bris, who has worked miracles these past two years, was under pressure.

Things, however, could not have started worse for Le Bris. Though Granit Xhaka has not shown last season’s form in these challenging opening months, the game strategy was built around him, so to see the Sunderland captain hobbling off after three minutes was symptomatic of how things have gone for the Wearsiders.

Recent findings suggest that “He felt something in the final sprint of the warm-up,” Le Bris explained. “We don’t know how bad it is.”.

He is not the kind of coach, though, who will bemoan bad fortune. Le Bris sent on Jules Ahoka to replace Xhaka and watched as he, along with colleagues in red and white, set about trampling all over Chelsea’s intentions with incessant hard work.

Recent findings suggest that yet there was more to it. Sunderland can play, either intricately or directly, and a lovely move in the 12th minute needed a desperate, sliding intervention from Pep Chavarría’s to stop Trai Hume’s volley sliding in at the far post.

In the next attack, another Chemsdine Talbi cross – the Moroccan having been found by a peach of a pass from goalkeeper Robin Roefs – invited Brobbey to inflict maximum damage, but the Dutchman made a hash of his opportunity.

Recent findings suggest that so close for Brobbey! 🤏 Sunderland almost take the lead against Chelsea. https://t.co/CUE6jHbPH2.

The momentum could have changed completely in the 23rd minute. Alonso, his players and staff were convinced they would be given a penalty after Cole Palmer tumbled when his legs tangled with Luke O’Nien but, after a lengthy delay, VAR Nick Hopton felt there was no case to answer.

Hopton was involved again in the 33rd minute but, as Alonso said, Chelsea only had themselves to blame. Colwill simply could not contain Brobbey when he began marauding, grappling, grabbing and clipping the Dutchman’s heels. Le Fée did the rest, sending Mike Penders the wrong way.

Enzo Le Fee dispatches the penalty as Sunderland take the lead against Chelsea! 🔴⚪️ https://t.co/cCtYsHVWB9.

It has been revealed that from that point, Chelsea were in trouble, no matter how many changes Alonso made. They huffed, puffed, but nothing worked. They had come up against a red-and-white wall, fortified by constant backing from the stands, and the west Londoners were never going to knock it down.

One incident, as the clock ticked towards 90 minutes, encapsulated everything good about this Sunderland display when O’Nien chased down substitute Geovany Quenda to make a challenge. Another moment of defending from Thomas Meunier on Morgan Rogers was exceptional.

In a recent development, “You could see our identity and our togetherness and the way we managed the game,” said Le Bris, who was booked when hectoring referee Jarred Gillett. “These three points were critical. It was a struggle at times to manage situations. We highlighted as a group real heart.”.

And nobody did that more than Brobbey. No wonder Le Bris will be hoping Xavi Hernández, the Netherlands head coach, handles him with care over the next 10 days. On this form, he will be the fuel that drives Sunderland’s quest for survival.

“You know when you come here in this stadium it will be a difficult game and that was the matter tonight. We knew it would be tough, we are disappointed we lost the game. At one point it went very fast from side to side. Sometimes we had to control. With 11 behind the ball it is difficult to find the spaces.”.

On where Chelsea stand ahead of the international break...

“For me it wasn’t a penalty. He barely touched him, I think it was the other way round. He grabbed him.”.

This season Xabi Alonso has been determined to ensure that that is not the case this season.

Sunday’s opponents Sunderland ran Chelsea off the park twice last season. Only once, in the 36th Premier League game of the campaign against Liverpool, did Chelsea cover more distance than their opposition.

That Sunderland did the double over Chelsea last season.

A last-minute winner from Chemsdine Talbi grabbed the points at Stamford Bridge, before Sunderland won 2-1, without breaking sweat, at the Stadium of Light on the last day of the campaign.

Recent findings suggest that those victories, and the manner of them, underlined what a season it was for Regis Le Bris’s men. How they wish this campaign started as that one ended.

Today is must-win match: for both sides.

For Sunderland that argument is easy to make – they are bottom of the Premier League, are without a win since August and for morale, if nothing else need at least a point, though three is really what the doctor orders.

For Chelsea – fourth in the table and with three wins in their past four league outings – the argument that this is a must-win game is harder to make, but bear with me here...

Facing a Sunderland team who are suffering from the worst of both worlds – blunt in attack and pitiful in defence (what a difference from last season...) and have proven all too easy to beat (as their 2-0 home defeat Zagreb illustrated on Thursday) – the west Londoners are expected to win. Fail to return to the capital with the three points and there will once again be question marks over Xabi Alonso’s side. They are flaky and flashy in equal measure, able to play and win well in spurts, but once again unable to mount sustained pressure needed for a title challenge and forced to battle it out for the hope of a top-four spot at best. Those will be the arguments raised should they not win this afternoon.

The hosts doubtless wish that their ‘issues’ were as golden as today’s opposition. For Trai Hume, who scored in this fixture last season, the Sunderland players are at fault for the sorry start to the season and he wants to put right the wrongs so far, starting today.

Industry observers note that “I couldn’t tell you what’s changed. We thought we’d addressed it after the Leeds game, where we were aggressive, strong, but we go out there tonight and see the old habits of the start of the season. Everything’s a bit laboured, and it’s something the staff can’t fix, it’s on us as players,” Hume said.

Industry observers note that “We’re still together as a club, as a team. I think the run of form we’re on, it would be easy to think we’re not, but we are. We are really upset with how we’ve been playing, and the results don’t lie. We haven’t been good enough and we know that. We have to address that.”.

The England international has established himself as one of the Premier League’s most promising left-backs, but Newcastle’s reluctance to lose him could make negotiations difficult.

According to a TEAMtalk report, Liverpool have enquired about Hall’s situation and want to stay informed about his future at St James’ Park.

The 22-year-old previously attracted considerable interest from Manchester United, but he committed his long-term future to Newcastle in September by signing a new contract until 2031.

The Magpies have no intention of letting their defensive star leave, although sources indicate that an offer exceeding £66 million could bring them to the negotiating table.

Manchester United remain interested in securing his services, meaning Liverpool could face competition from their Premier League rivals if they decide to pursue a deal.

Liverpool are understood to have concerns about Milos Kerkez’s development since his £40 million arrival from Bournemouth in 2025.

The Hungarian international has struggled to deliver consistent performances, prompting the Anfield hierarchy to consider alternatives at left-back.

Recent findings suggest that hall could be an attractive addition because of his Premier League experience, defensive qualities and ability to contribute going forward. His homegrown status would also make him a valuable acquisition for Liverpool.

However, Newcastle’s determination to retain the defender and his long-term contract make a January transfer unlikely.

Liverpool are expected to continue monitoring his situation, with next summer potentially providing a more realistic opportunity to explore a deal.

Hall remains an important part of Newcastle’s long-term intends, and the Magpies will certainly demand a substantial financial commitment before considering his departure.

Manchester United have triggered a one-year extension on Bruno Fernandes’ contract, ending Milan’s hopes of signing him on a free transfer next summer.

It has been revealed that according to The Athletic, the club captain is now tied to Old Trafford until June 2028. Fernandes had been entering the final year of his deal and recently confirmed that talks over a newly introduced contract had been put on hold, with both sides wanting to focus on improving results.

By exercising the option, United have stopped the 32-year-old from negotiating with foreign clubs from 1 January, when he would otherwise have been free to agree a pre-contract.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, manchester United are in talks over a move to sign Calvin Bassey from Fulham in January. The 26-year-old has emerged as United's top defensive target for the winter transfer window, as Mauricio Pochettino tries to strengthen his squad.

United are in desperate need to add to their back-line after conceding the most goals (36) across Europe's top five leagues in all competitions this season. They have kept just one clean sheet in 17 matches and that came in the 4-0 rout over Azerbaijani minnows Sabah back in September.

It's a defensive record that must improve if Pochettino wants to have a positive impact at Old Trafford, and work has started on bolstering the back-line in January. According to The Athletic, talks are taking place to understand the conditions for a potential transfer for Fulham defender Bassey, who has impressed in the Premier League for a number of seasons.

Recent findings suggest that the Nigerian was rewarded with the captain's armband at Craven Cottage in the summer and has grown into status since Alvaro Arbeloa's arrival. Indeed, he is Fulham's first-choice centre-back now and the Whites are pushing to extend his contract.

Bassey is an excellent one-v-one defender and is strong at driving with the ball. He would strengthen United's back-line should they decide to bring him to the club in January, though Fulham are determined to keep him.

In a recent development, everton's Jarrad Branthwaite and Brentford's Nathan Collins are among the other Premier League defenders United are interested in. But the Reds are conscious about Branthwaite's injury record and feel they could be priced out of a move for Collins.

In a recent development, despite United's interest in Bassey, Branthwaite and Collins, the Reds should make Borussia Dortmund's Joane Gadou their priority centre-back target for the January transfer window. The 19-year-old produced a stellar performance for the German side in their 1-1 draw against Arsenal in the Champions League on Tuesday and has been a revelation this season.

Gadou, who joined Dortmund in a £20million deal from Red Bull Salzburg in May, was Dortmund's standout performer at the Emirates Stadium and was unfortunate not to be awarded with the Player of the Match prize, which went to Noni Madueke.

Starting on the right side of a back three, the 6ft 5in wonderkid won eight out of his 10 duels, and made two tackles, one interception, seven clearances and two blocks. He ensured Christos Tzolis had an evening to forget on Arsenal's left.

According to recent reports, he is an excellent one-v-one defender, is good at reading the game and has unbelievable athleticism and pace to recover when needed. As well as that, he is strong in the air, winning both of his aerial duels against Arsenal.

According to recent reports, although Gadou impressed from a defensive point-of-view, he was as good, if not better, on the ball. Indeed, the France Under 21s international provided a moment of magic leading to Dortmund's second-half equaliser in north London.

Picking up the ball in his own half, Gadou drove past Tzolis and at least 40 yards up field before picking out a pass, playing a composed ball through to Maximilian Beier, who took one touch and buried a low shot past Kepa Arrizabalaga.

It's an assist that has gone viral on social media, with Dortmund sharing it and getting more than 500,000 views, while others have lauded praise on the 'unbelievable' and 'insane' teenage defender who is catching the eye.

Recent findings suggest that along with the assist, Gadou progressed the ball on several other occasions. He completed 22 out of his 22 passes, made three accurate passes into the final third and had three progressive passes. In total, Gadou had 50 touches and one shot.

Gadou's profile is unique. Les Parisien described him as "tall, athletic, and not clumsy with the ball at his feet", adding that he is "efficient in both penalty areas." Meanwhile, France Under 17s head coach Jean-Luc Vannuchi said Gadou is a "force of nature", saying that he "combines power and speed", as well as being "interesting with his use of the ball.".

In a recent development, he is both "capable of playing short [and] playing long", according to Vannuchi. Yohan Cabaye, the former Newcastle United and Crystal Palace midfielder, highlighted Gadou's efficiency in one-on-one situations and above-average speed.

Sources indicate that flashscore gave Gadou a 8.2/10 rating for his performance against Arsenal - the second highest on the pitch behind Madueke (8.5) - and his progress has not gone unnoticed. BILD have reported that United, Liverpool and Arsenal are monitoring Gadou's progress, with Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain among the others interested.

But Dortmund are not fazed by the attention Gadou is getting, due to the fact he is under contract until 2031 and he has no release clause attached. The Bundesliga outfit are not considering a sale for less than £69m.

It has been revealed that despite that, United should pay what it takes to land Gadou in January. He is a generational talent and they will regret not moving first to sign him. The Frenchman will turn out to be one of the best defenders in world football in the future.

While Bassey, for example, is a more cost-effective option given the fact United won't have to spend more than £30m on him, he is seven years older than Gadou and doesn't have the same potential or even resale value.

Gadou has the talent to become the most expensive defender ever, and for £69m, United would be getting someone that could at least double their value, if not more, should he keep on the same trajectory.

He has made 17 appearances for Dortmund this season and has been a firm fixture in Niko Kovac's first XI. Before someone else does, United need to move fast to land him in January, and he should be their first-choice centre-back target.

Gadou and Leny Yoro could be United's long-term centre-back partnership. Even for now, that is what it would be if the Reds were to land the 2007-born sensation in January, with Harry Maguire and Matthijs de Ligt as back-up.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that aerial scenery of Hengqin Free Trade Zone, China. Credit: Weiming Xie/Shutterstock.

Recent findings suggest that two-thirds of the world’s population will be living in cities by 2050, according to the latest estimates by the United Nations. Coinciding with the mass movement of people into urban areas is the rapid integration of technology into many of those spaces. From automated subterranean waste-collection systems to driverless vehicle zones, these ‘smart-city’ solutions are changing the way that people live, work and move through their environments.

Some cities are embracing these technological advances at a much faster pace than others. Places such as Beijing, Helsinki, London and Singapore stand out for the way they are integrating smart-city technology into existing infrastructure and services.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

Sources indicate that other cities are emerging with these technologies integral to their operations from their inception. But as the examples of Songdo in South Korea and Hengqin in China illustrate, building smart infrastructure from scratch is only half the challenge: these places must also attract and retain the research and innovation talent needed to develop, operate and improve it. It’s a ‘chicken-and-egg’ problem, claims Songdo-based urban-planning researcher, Dakota McCarty: talent follows world-class universities and thriving economic zones, which need a critical mass of expertise and investment to be attractive.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The European Union and Indonesia signed a free trade deal on Saturday, describing it as a new chapter in economic relations between the two sides.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The European Union and Indonesia signed a free trade deal on Saturday, describing it as a new chapter in economic relations between the two sides.

"This is one of the most ambitious deals the European Union has concluded in Asia," Ursula von der Leyen, president of the European Commission, remarked at the signing ceremony on Saturday.

"Together, we represent a market of 730 million people," she added.

The Indonesia-European Union Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) and the additional Investment Protection Agreement (IPA) are designed to reduce trade barriers and attract investment in strategic sectors such as electric vehicles, electronics, and pharmaceuticals.

The agreement comes after almost 10 years of negotiations and is part of a wider series of trade deals by the EU.

The bloc hopes to reduce its reliance on individual economic partners as trade with both China and the US has become more difficult in recent years.

Von der Leyen also stressed the importance of international cooperation, saying that "in a time when others are closing their doors, we keep ours open.".

The deal sees tariffs on about 98% of EU exports to Indonesia to be done away with. The EU estimates that European companies could save more than €600 million (around $658 million) per year.

In a recent development, "The benefits for our exporters are concrete and measurable," Indonesian Minister of Economic Affairs Airlangga Hartarto noted, hailing a "fresh chapter" in economic relations with the EU. He said the deal would benefit his country’s main exports to Europe, including palm oil, footwear and textiles.

Palm oil and deforestation had been major stumbling blocks during the negotiations, and the agreement includes mechanisms for cooperation on regulatory and sustainability issues as well as a dedicated protocol on palm oil to address environmental concerns.

The EU parliament is now expected to greenlight the deal while Indonesian authorities will also complete the ratification process so it can enter into force in 2027.

It's far too early to make sweeping conclusions about the Premier League season or individual players, although a number of stars at the likes of Manchester United, Manchester City and Tottenham Hotspur have certainly had disappointing starts to the new campaign.

Not all of these objectives are off the table, although all three clubs will be somewhat frustrated with how they've performed, with particular players underwhelming.

However, these aren't the only clubs that have flattered to deceive, with the likes of Chelsea, Aston Villa and Sunderland all enduring difficult campaigns — let down by out-of-form individuals whom they'd expect more from.

With that remarked, GMS have ranked the top 20 most disappointing Premier League players of the 2026/27 season so far.

Coming in at number 20 is Leeds United's Harry Wilson, who signed from Fulham over the summer on a free transfer. While the lack of a transfer fee means the Yorkshire club can stomach a disappointing campaign from Wilson, it doesn't make his lacklustre performances any less frustrating. After scoring 11 goals and providing eight assists across all competitions for the Cottagers last term, he was viewed as an incredible pick-up for Leeds, yet he's 11 games into his Whites career, and he's yet to get off the mark. The Chelsea loanee has been nothing short of disastrous at Selhurst Park, as the Eagles currently sit rock bottom of the Premier League, having shipped 27 goals — more than anyone else.

It has been revealed that mykhailo Mudryk's fortunes at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium haven't been much better. In a recent development, dominik Szoboszlai has disappointed for Liverpool, but in a completely different way from all of the above. The Hungarian was the Reds' talisman last season and was expected to ascend to another level as the Merseyside club's definitive best player after the departure of Mohamed Salah. Top 20 Most Disappointing Premier League Players 2026/27.

That cannot be said of Senne Lammens, who was highly rated based on his debut season at Old Trafford, and has since seen his performances decline significantly. A number of high-profile errors have cost United goals and points.

Across Manchester, another goalkeeper is having a dire season. Gianluigi Donnarumma, widely regarded as one of the world's best shot-stoppers, has been off the boil in this department this season, adding to his calamitous work with the ball at his feet.

According to recent reports, the Italian's teammate, Marc Guehi, has been equally catastrophic. So dependable last term, the former Crystal Palace captain has seemingly been rocked by Enzo Maresca's less-stable system and has subsequently made an array of mistakes leading to goals.

Top 20 Most Disappointing Premier League Players 2026/27.

The numbers show that Bruno Fernandes has still been one of the most creative players in the Premier League this season. The extent to which he's been poor has likely been overblown, but that's not to say he hasn't been extremely disappointing based on the heights he hit last term as Player of the Season. He hasn't been able to carry United's attack in the same way through his playmaking, and that's not to mention some of his questionable antics as the captain of the Red Devils.

Sandro Tonali was one of the summer window's biggest acquisitions, arriving at Tottenham from Newcastle for £100 million. While it's not his fault that he was bought for such a significant sum, he's certainly not justified Spurs' investment with his performances. He's played at a respectable level, but he hasn't looked remotely capable of being the talismanic figure De Zerbi's team needs to lead them towards a Champions League place.

United have obviously been the biggest underperformer this season, and this list unsurprisingly reflects this. Lisandro Martinez comes in at number three, producing several dismal performances that have contributed to the Red Devils conceding 23 goals in 11 matches. He's been all at sea positionally and in possession, whilst his small frame has seen him physically dominated by imposing forwards. Let's not forget he also publicly called out the club's summer signings and the board, despite being a disaster himself.

Recent findings suggest that youri Tielemans has been even more disappointing than his teammate. The Belgian was expected to finally provide United with a tempo-setting metronome in the middle of the park, but has instead been a liability, with his limited physical attributes leaving the north-west team's defence exposed in transition throughout matches.

Finally, the Premier League's most disappointing player so far in the 2026/27 season has to go to Enzo Fernandez. Acquired for a staggering £125 million, he's been largely diabolical for the Citizens, not translating his excellent form from last season to his fresh club. Three months in, and it's already clear that Maresca's best midfield doesn't involve the Argentine.

He cannot play alongside Rayan Cherki, as this leaves Elliot Anderson exposed at the base of City's midfield. Thus, Maresca has to play Ayyoub Bouaddi alongside Anderson, forming a double pivot, and Cherki's superior output to Fernandez means the World Cup winner should generally be left on the bench.

A Russian helicopter is suspected of violating Finnish airspace, the Nordic country's Ministry of Defense noted Saturday.

The incident happened a few hours after a drone attack left a Russian cargo ship ablaze in the Gulf of Finland, the easternmost part of the Baltic Sea.

Recent findings suggest that according to Finland's Defense Ministry, the incursion happened at 12:34 p.m. local time (10:34 UTC/GMT) off the town of Loviisa, on the southern coast.

"This alleged airspace violation may be linked to rescue or surveillance operations carried out by Finland following damage sustained by a cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland," public broadcaster YLE cited Defense Minister Antti Hakkanen as saying.

The ministry added the helicopter could have penetrated up to 4.1 kilometers (2.5 miles) into Finnish territory.

Earlier Saturday, Finland — one of NATO's newest members — mentioned a Russian cargo ship heading for Russia's Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad caught fire after being struck by drones in the Gulf of Finland.

The Finnish military said the Sparta II was damaged ⁠west ⁠of Russia's Gogland island, about 40 kilometers (25 miles) from Finland's coast, and later drifted into Finnish territorial waters.

Finnish ‌Border ​Guard Commander Ilja Iljin later told YLE that the vessel, which is known to have links to the Russian military, was struck by Ukrainian  drones while in Russian waters.

"At the moment, ​there is no confirmed information ⁠about ​what cargo ​is on board, ​but it ‌cannot be ruled out ​that ⁠there is military materiel on ⁠board," ​Iljin remarked.

The ship is on a US sanctions list, according to a search of the Open Sanctions website.

The Border Guard later said the crew of the Sparta II was evacuating into a life raft and rescue boat.

"The [Ukraine] war is spilling over into our neighbouring areas," wrote Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo on X.

Ukraine has the right to fight against the aggressor," he added.

The Finnish government has put temporary curbs on aviation and maritime traffic in the eastern Gulf of Finland.

The Defense Ministry remarked Finland had informed its allies about the incident.

In a recent development, luke Shaw is nearing a return to full fitness, however, and is expected to take back that spot soon, after missing the last seven weeks with a muscle problem. Despite that, Shaw has struggled even when available and United should look to upgrade in the transfer window.

According to Sport Witness, United are showing interest in Sporting left-back Maxi Araujo. It's understood the Reds have been monitoring the Uruguay international for a number of months now, and, of course, saw him up close at the Estadio Jose Alvalade on Wednesday.

Sources indicate that araujo has a £67million release clause in his contract, but United could get him for less in January. As well as that, he is believed to be 'very open' about making the move to Old Trafford and has previously expressed his desire to play in the Premier League.

According to recent reports, it could be a smart signing, but United should avoid Araujo and instead target someone else. While the 26-year-old did win Sporting's second spot-kick as he was fouled by Senne Lammens and was an attacking threat, he has some substantial flaws to his game.

It has been revealed that indeed, in the draw against United, Araujo lost possession NINE times, completing just 86 per cent of his passes (38/46) and having one out of four successful dribbles. He didn't make a single accurate pass into the box and completed just one successful cross.

Alongside that, Araujo's defending flattered to deceive. He won just 42 per cent (8/19) of his duels, one tackle and committed three fouls. The ex-Puebla and Toluca man started as a left wing-back and often got caught out with Amad Diallo having joy on that side.

While he can be strong going forward, Araujo does struggle defensively and has proven that on a number of occasions this season. None more so than in the 3-2 defeat to LASK in the Champions League last month, where he could have done better for all three goals. He didn't stop the cross for LASK's first, while both the second and third came down his side.

Considering that and the fact United have conceded the most goals (36) in Europe's top five leagues across all competitions this season, the Reds need a more defensive-minded left-back and Newcastle United's Lewis Hall would be perfect.

Sources indicate that the Athletic have reported that United remain interested in Hall, and although it could be difficult for them to persuade Newcastle to sell in January, the Reds need to do all they can to sign him. The England international is one of the best left-sided defenders in the Premier League right now and would be an exceptional addition, even if he is expensive.

Industry observers note that defensively, there are not too many better than Hall about. He produced an impressive performance to keep Lamine Yamal quiet in England's famous 3-2 win against Spain earlier this month, and has been a nemesis for many a right-winger in recent times.

It has been revealed that he can attack as well. Indeed, in 113 appearances for Newcastle, Hall has directly contributed to 13 goals. Earlier this season, Hall found the net in a 2-1 win at Hull City and grabbed an assist in a 2-2 draw at home against Bournemouth.

United should go all out to bring Hall to Old Trafford. He should be their first-choice target with Araujo and Antonee Robinson behind. Despite their league position, the Reds should be targeting the best in class - and Hall is just that.

Former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe heaped praise on the "outstanding" Hall last season, despite leaving him out of the starting line-up to face Arsenal. “Lewis is an outstanding player and you never for any second doubt his qualities and what he can bring to the team," Howe said, when asked the reason behind Dan Burn's inclusion in the team at left-back.

In a recent development, meanwhile, Pochettino worked with Hall for a brief period at Chelsea and wished him well as he moved to Newcastle. Acknowledging his potential, the Argentine said: “He was unlucky that he could not play [more], but he has a good future and I hope he can settle well there.”.

Thomas Tuchel hailed Hall's progress during the recent international break, saying he made a "big impression" on the England team.

Swansea City have debuted an internal investigation after an inappropriate image of one of its players was shared on social media.

While Swansea blueprint to speak to the player to establish the key facts behind the image, there is also a legal side that cannot be ignored.

In England and Wales it is a criminal offence to share naked or intimate photos without consent under Section 66B of the Sexual Offences Act 2003.

Should an investigation determine the image has been tampered with, including AI-generated or manipulated 'deepfakes,' which was one of the allegations on social media on Wednesday night, that too is a criminal act under the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025.

Bosses at soccer team Bayern Munich have publicly questioned whether young Germany international Jamal Musiala's contract is valid in view of a debilitating neurological condition.
