NWSL announces upcoming player development rule to incentivize youth investment, aims for further expansion

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (979 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the biggest week on the NWSL calendar is here as the buildup towards the 2026 NWSL Championship is underway.
  • Recent findings suggest that this year, the commissioner welcomed media to the NWSL Championship in Washington, D.C., and celebrated record ticket sales, attendance, and future expansion ahead of Saturday night's championship between the Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current, live on CBS at 8 p.m.
  • The commissioner introduced the fresh player development rule.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the biggest week on the NWSL calendar is here as the buildup towards the 2026 NWSL Championship is underway. An awards show, countless events, and media days were all on the agenda ahead of Saturday's major game. That included the annual state of the league by commissioner Jessica Berman on Thursday.

Recent findings suggest that this year, the commissioner welcomed media to the NWSL Championship in Washington, D.C., and celebrated record ticket sales, attendance, and future expansion ahead of Saturday night's championship between the Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current, live on CBS at 8 p.m. ET. She also unveiled a few new league rules and future match events.

Here are the new things coming to NWSL:.

The commissioner introduced the fresh player development rule. While the league previously submitted paperwork for a potential future second=division league, conversation and planning around that is presently paused with the upcoming 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup and efforts to grow NWSL in other ways.

It has been revealed that "As we grow from 16 to 18 teams in 2028, we know that we have to prioritize the pipeline, not just the pipeline of players, but the pipeline of talent that supports the players in the daily training environment. One of the things that makes the United States so uniquely positioned in the global women's soccer landscape is the depth of that potential pipeline," said Berman in her opening remarks.

"That's why today we're announcing the NWSL Player Development Rule. It's an important step in strengthening the pathway to professional soccer for the next generation of players. The rule creates actual incentives for clubs to invest in identifying, developing, and retaining young talent, and it gives the clubs the flexibility to design their programs in the way that makes sense with their sporting philosophies.".

More information and the types of incentives will roll out for clubs as the newly introduced player development rule goes into effect, but it is another step in future roster-building for clubs now alongside general player signings, transfers, the High Impact Player rule, and the Under-18 mechanism.

According to recent reports, the addition of the rule is paving the way for more support staff and systems in place. The commissioner also confirmed the fresh NWSL Sporting Executive Program, meant to provide more support for club leadership development. The inaugural set of leadership includes six executives from the league who will participate in the program.

It has been revealed that "Developing the future of the sport is not just limited to the players; it's also about the technical staff who surround those players each and every day ... this is a first-of-its-kind program invested in talent, and it was curated and developed in collaboration with U.S. Soccer and FIFA. This latest year-long initiative will provide sporting executives at our clubs with curated, specialized education, mentorship, and leadership development opportunities tailored around the unique demands of our league and the women's professional game," she stated.

The NWSL commissioner then unveiled the future site of the next NWSL Challenge Cup. The 2027 NWSL Challenge Cup will take place in Austin, Texas, next summer.

Industry observers note that the tournament has evolved since its first iteration as a placeholder for the COVID-19-affected season and is now a unique one-off marquee match between top clubs, typically the NWSL Shield titleholders and the NWSL Championship winners. In years where one club wins both, the game is a rematch of the previous NWSL Championship match.

"Following the success of this year's Challenge Cup in Columbus, where we took the event to a neutral site to give an opportunity to introduce the NWSL to a newly introduced community," she said.

The 2026 NWSL Challenge Cup was between 2025 NWSL Shield winners Kansas City Current and 2025 NWSL Championship winners Gotham FC. The 2026 competition was held in Columbus, Ohio. The state will now welcome its first NWSL franchise in 2028 alongside another expansion club in Atlanta.

Recent findings suggest that fans will undoubtedly make the connection and wonder if there is a future where an NWSL club calls Austin home. Presently, there are three NWSL clubs in California and only one in Texas, the Houston Dash.

"We're really excited to create another special experience for our fans and our players while making the NWSL a place that can invite new audiences," Berman stated about heading to Austin.

Industry observers note that commissioner Berman celebrated the league's recent return to the nation's capital for another NWSL Championship. The city hosted the 2022 event and now returns four years later with more attention on the league, the clubs, and its players than ever before.

It has been revealed that "Today, we're bigger, stronger, more visible, and more ambitious than ever before, and the next five years are going to redefine what's possible. We have an extraordinary opportunity in front of us, and we intend to seize it," she stated.

It has been revealed that two incoming clubs set for 2028 and latest player roster rules are just the beginning of NWSL's next chapter. There's still the potential for more clubs on the horizon, and current clubs Houston Dash and Racing Louisville are in the process of vetting for a sale to new ownership as franchise entry fees into the league are booming to new heights.

And of course, there is still the biggest game of the year to play on Saturday.

"The Washington Spirit are back in the championship for the third consecutive year, determined to bring home that title. And standing in their way is the Kansas City Current, with its own ambitions to win a championship after winning the Shield in 2025. These are two exceptional clubs, two incredibly passionate fan base, and the championship is still to be decided, [we're] very excited about the rest of this week.".

#151611. Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch' is more alive than you'd expect

Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch' is more alive than you'd expect

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (940 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rembrandt van Rijn's "The Night Watch" is one of the most famous paintings of the Dutch Golden Age.
  • In the painting, Rembrandt made dramatic use of light and shadow to guide the viewer's eye to key figures.
  • Beyond the sense of movement featured in "The Night Watch," the painting itself is also alive in a way that's rarely taken into consideration — through the microscopic organisms living on the canvas.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rembrandt van Rijn's "The Night Watch" is one of the most famous paintings of the Dutch Golden Age. Amsterdam's Rijksmuseum, where the work is on display, hails the artist's 1642 masterpiece as "the turning point in his career and as the superlative example of his creative genius.".

In the painting, Rembrandt made dramatic use of light and shadow to guide the viewer's eye to key figures. And unlike static group portraits typical of his era, the artist depicted Amsterdam's civic guards in mid-action, as they prepare to march out.

Beyond the sense of movement featured in "The Night Watch," the painting itself is also alive in a way that's rarely taken into consideration — through the microscopic organisms living on the canvas.

The research project "The Night Watch Lives" explores exactly that question: What kinds of life forms inhabit the surface of the famous painting?

The study is a collaborative scientific and exhibition project between the Rijksmuseum and ARTIS-Micropia — an Amsterdam museum dedicated to the world of microorganisms.

In a recent development, it's part of the broader "Operation Night Watch" restoration and research project described as the "biggest and most wide-ranging ever study and restoration of Rembrandt's most famous painting," started in 2019. Conservators and scientists in this project have been examining every aspect of Rembrandt's masterpiece using cutting-edge technology, seeking new insights into its materials, condition and history — and now, its microbiome.

It has been revealed that the idea behind "The Night Watch Lives" was to "put microbes in a positive spotlight," Eline van Bloois, who led the research, told DW. "Honestly, if you're asking me — I'm a microbiologist, so I'm biased of course — but they really deserve more positive attention.".

Over a period of six months, van Bloois will be taking samples once a month directly from the famous painting at the Rijksmuseum, accompanied by the people working on the restoration of "The Night Watch.".

Using small sterile discs gently pressed against selected areas of the painting, the samples collect microscopic material from both varnished and unvarnished sections.

These samples are then cultivated in laboratories, allowing previously invisible microbes to grow into visible colonies that can be studied and identified.

At the "The Night Watch Lives" exhibition, visitors can view Petri dishes containing the cultivated microbial colonies. A life-size reproduction of Rembrandt's masterpiece also reveals where the samples were taken, and which microorganisms were found there.

It has been revealed that at the exhibition's opening on November 11, the installation included the findings of two of van Bloois' sampling sessions. Four more will be added over the coming months, allowing the museum's visitors to follow the results of the study as it unfolds.

That means the exhibition's visitors "will be figuring out what I've found as I'm figuring it out myself," explains the microbiologist. "We really take them through that journey with us.".

People often fear microbes or associate them with disease, even though the vast majority of these microscopic organisms are actually harmless or vital to human survival.

Some of the organisms found on the painting "are very commonly found on human skin, for instance, and they're a healthy part of the microbiome; most humans actually have these bacteria with them," indicates van Bloois, adding that the presence of these microbes on the painting made sense, since humans are often near the work.

But another bacterium stood out in the samples: Microbacterium saccharophilum, a species first identified at a sugar refinery in Japan in 2013. How this microorganism ended up on the Dutch "Night Watch," or when, is a guessing game.

According to recent reports, "It's part of the fun and part of the frustration in microbiology. You cannot ask the microbes where they originate from," indicates van Bloois. "It would make our lives a bit easier, but it's also fun to have a little bit of a mystery.".

The samples also revealed bacteria from soil, often found in plant roots. Could these organisms somehow harm the painting? Could plants start growing on the work?

Van Bloois explains why this is highly unlikely: On the painting, the bacteria can form inactive spores, but for the study, the researcher "provided them with all the nutrients and the right temperature and the right humidity that allowed them to grow again.".

Still, studying these organisms may eventually contribute to understanding how paintings age, how environmental conditions affect cultural heritage, and how museums can better preserve priceless works of art.

As to whether the microorganisms could date back to Rembrandt's time, the microbiologist claims that's also "highly unlikely" — but here again, microbes cannot reveal their origin story.

As part of the larger "Operation Night Watch" team, van Bloois is definitely inspired by this "group effort where everyone is just really enthusiastic about telling these stories and adding to the knowledge surrounding 'The Night Watch.'".

The microbiological samples revealed by the laboratory process resemble abstract art in miniature: colorful clusters, delicate textures and intricate patterns created by living organisms.

And as the study is unfolding publicly, it also feels like an artistic performance of its own.

The project also perfectly embodies the full name of the museum where the exhibition is held: Natura Artis Magistra, a Latin phrase that translates to "nature is the teacher of art and science," as the microbiologist points out: "It's really cool to see science and art all come together in this project.".

The exhibition "The Night Watch Lives" runs at ARTIS-Micropia in Amsterdam until the end of May 2027.

MLS Cup bracket predictions: Lionel Messi's Inter Miami set for repeat?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (994 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, it's time for some brackets as the MLS Cup playoffs are upon us.
  • In a recent development, while the Wild Card round is a one-off, win-or-go-home match, the first round is a best-of-three series with games going to a penalty shootout if tied.
  • The Seattle Sounders come into this postseason in a tough spot.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it's time for some brackets as the MLS Cup playoffs are upon us. With the Wild Card round kicking off on Thursday night, 18 teams (still too many) will enter the gauntlet that is the playoffs. All eyes will be on Nashville SC, who have a first-round bye after winning the Supporters' Shield and setting a latest MLS regular-season points record with 77 points. However, when it comes down to it, anyone can fall in a one-off match, as being successful in the regular season is a different proposition than doing so in the postseason.

In a recent development, while the Wild Card round is a one-off, win-or-go-home match, the first round is a best-of-three series with games going to a penalty shootout if tied. That can change the calculus a bit, especially for teams getting an early goal in the first game, since there are still two more chances to advance. But since there are playoffs, that also means that we have to predict the bracket, so let's get to it.

The Seattle Sounders come into this postseason in a tough spot. While they've become a team that can't be counted out of MLS Cup contention, they enter the playoffs without one of their best defenders. Center back Jackson Ragen was suspended for two games following a disciplinary review for his challenge on Los Angeles FC's Jacob Shaffelburg. While the Sounders have returned to health, this opens the door for Real Salt Lake to get out of the Wild Card round.

In Orlando, this is one of the matchups of the entire playoffs as Evander and Antoine Griezmann will battle in a match where defense is optional. Both teams had higher ambitions heading into the season, so for the loser, it could have major implications. But after winning Newcomer of the Year, Griezmann, alongside Orlando's strong attack, will prove to be too much to handle for Cincinnati as we head to the first round of the playoffs proper.

The parity in MLS this season, especially in the Western Conference, is real. You could tell me that anyone would come out of the West, and it's believable. Vancouver may be the team to beat, but needing to replace Sebastian Berhalter and Andres Cubas midseason did hurt the squad. Jesper Sorensen has done plenty to keep Vancouver afloat, but they're still vulnerable, although that'll be more of an issue in later rounds depending on how the bracket shakes out. St. Louis City SC have already exceeded expectations by winning the U.S. Open Cup, and if Alexandru Matan is on his game, they may be unbeatable, but they can run hot and cold. Add in Bruce Arena still evolving with the league and the cardiac kids of Dallas (and of course the brilliance of Petar Musa), and that brings us to the advancing sides. I would apologize to Los Angeles FC, but post-Steve Cherundolo, this is a side that has faltered, and a long look needs to be taken at the squad following the season to move forward.

Recent findings suggest that in the East, we're in B.J. Callaghan's world. Los Angeles FC are the last team to do the double of winning the Supporters' Shield and MLS Cup, and it's a tough thing for Nashville to do, but this team has only allowed 25 goals in a full season. They can score, they can grind a game to a halt, and they have so many ways to give the opposition fits. In a best-of-three, good luck getting past them. Speaking of slowing a game down, the New England Revolution are a worst-case matchup for the fighting Cavan Sullivans of Philadelphia. Joshua Wynder has stabilized the defense in front of Matt Turner, and while the Revolution may not have a high ceiling as constructed, the floor is so high in this unique setup. Charlotte facing Chicago might as well be a coin flip. Then there's Miami facing Columbus. Like the Union, the Crew can win because their attacking upside is so high, and Miami are a flawed team, but Lionel Messi is still doing Lionel Messi things. As long as that's the case, I'm rarely going to bet against the Herons.

Now the playoffs really are getting underway. These are one-off games where the best of the best are going up against each other. San Jose's run comes to an end here, while St. Louis and Dallas fight in an evenly matched clash to determine who else comes out of the Western Conference. Nashville's defense again puts up a suffocating performance to get past Charlotte, and Messi drives Inter Miami past the Revolution, setting up a fascinating set of conference finals.

Industry observers note that okay, I swear that this wasn't supposed to go chalk with three of the top four finishers in the regular season making it to the conference finals, but getting to the end of the season and saying that the good teams are actually good shouldn't be revolutionary. Thomas Muller and Brian White are enough to push the Whitecaps to the MLS Cup final, where the Eastern Conference yet again comes down to Messi versus Hany Mukhtar. Nashville may be the better-coached team, but Miami have found a way with their backs against the wall to produce a rematch of last season's MLS Cup final.

Participants: Vancouver Whitecaps, Inter MiamiWinners: Inter Miami.

Hey, it's Messi and Muller, just like we're having a top-tier Champions League matchup. It has been a playoff gauntlet, but the more things change, the more they stay the same. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the hottest ticket in the nation's capital is the biggest game of the year in the NWSL.
  • Recent findings suggest that the Spirit return to the final after settling for runner-up finishes in the previous two NWSL Championship events.
  • Traditionally, a neutral site is determined well before the NWSL Championship, and Audi Field was revealed back in June.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the hottest ticket in the nation's capital is the biggest game of the year in the NWSL. The Washington Spirit and the Kansas City Current will compete in the 2026 NWSL Championship, and both clubs have unfinished business. Kickoff is set for Nov. 21 at 8 p.m. ET on CBS and Paramount+.

Recent findings suggest that the Spirit return to the final after settling for runner-up finishes in the previous two NWSL Championship events. They lost 1-0 to the Orlando Pride in 2024 and fell short against Gotham FC in 2025. Now the Spirit have another chance at lifting the trophy, with a little extra incentive to do so, as the NWSL Championship returns to Washington, D.C.

Traditionally, a neutral site is determined well before the NWSL Championship, and Audi Field was revealed back in June.

The Kansas City Current are equally motivated to win the NWSL Championship after falling short in last year's playoffs. The club went on a record-setting regular-season run in 2025 and won the 2025 NWSL Shield but was eliminated in the quarterfinals. This year, they stormed through the postseason to reach the final game, looking for even more hardware.

Just a few days ago, some of the biggest stars were named to the NWSL's Best XI first team. Trinity Rodman and Croix Bethune were both honored on Wednesday night, and Bethune also took home her second Midfielder of the Year award. Rodman and the Spirit are looking for another NWSL Championship to add to their 2021 title, and Bethune -- who was traded from the Spirit in February -- is chasing history with the Current, who are still on the hunt for their first.

Here's everything you need to know about the massive game:.

Date: Saturday, Nov. 21 | Time: 8 p.m. ETLocation: Audi Field -- Washington, D.C.TV: CBS | Live stream: Paramount+Odds: Spirit +145 | Draw +215 | Current +160.

Industry observers note that the Washington Spirit's return to a third consecutive final came after a third-place finish in the regular season, in which the squad scored 43 goals and midseason arrivals quickly acclimated, proving a key difference. Now the club is back in the final for the fifth time in its history.

According to recent reports, head coach Adrian Gonzalez and his roster got off to a quick start in the playoffs and demolished the Portland Thorns 4-1 at home. Rodman scored twice, and new signings Melissa Bethi and Clara Luvanga also got on the scoresheet. The Spirit swiftly followed that up with a 2-1 come-from-behind victory over the Utah Royals, with goals by Sofia Cantore and Luvanga after the group conceded the opening goal just two minutes into the semifinal.

The Spirit's attacking trio of Rodman, Cantore and Luvanga is gelling at the right moment and looking dangerous in the postseason, with all three forwards on the scoresheet in the playoffs.

It has been revealed that "[The dynamic has] been great. Me and Soph have been able to build this connection a little bit longer, but it didn't take Clara very long. It's been amazing to see her grow and not only get comfortable but, like, get confident as well," Rodman noted of the relationship with her teammates.

According to recent reports, "I think playing at Audi [Field] obviously helps with that. But seeing her thrive, celebrate herself, has been really cool to see. But on top of that, the connection, I think, as a winger, you always want a center forward that you can work with and build off of and learn from. So it's been an amazing experience so far, and I'm hoping that we show that again on Saturday.".

Under first-year head coach Chris Armas, the group got off to a rocky start to the season but swiftly clawed its way to a fourth-place finish on the league table and co-led the league in goals scored (54) this season. The group has rallied around last year's short playoff appearance as a motivator, with several players saying this year is "personal" and citing the resilience they've shown. During some stretches of the year, the roster had to navigate varying injuries or player absences due to international duty: Temwa Chawinga came back from an injury and then participated in Women's AFCON in August; Bethune recently returned from a hip injury; and Michelle Cooper managed a lingering leg knock.

Recent findings suggest that "I'm feeling great. The vibes are good, which also helps. I think in some way, in some capacity, we're all tired. We played 30-plus games this year, but I think the vibes are so high that it doesn't even matter at this point. Like, we only have 90 minutes left in our season, so if we're crawling off that field, that's what we're gonna do," Cooper mentioned.

Sources indicate that "I'm glad everyone didn't come back healthy just in time for playoffs. Like we've had a couple months, two to three months, where all of us are healthy, which is nice. The level is constantly there. Even if something were to happen, we trust our bench. We trust the players that we have below us as well, and to be able to build the last two months and come into playoffs where everyone's kind of firing at the right time is exactly what we needed," she remarked.

In a recent development, the Spirit and the Current will compete in the NWSL Championship on Saturday at Audi Field. The winner will then compete for more silverware next summer in the 2027 NWSL Challenge Cup against the 2026 NWSL Shield holders, Gotham FC.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By LUKE POWER, SPORTS REPORTER and BEN WINSTANLEY and WILL PICKWORTH, SPORTS REPORTER and MILES STARFORTH.
  • Published: 15:09 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 19:33 EST, 26 November 2026.
  • Thomas Frank said he was happy to be 'back in the circus' at his Crystal Palace unveiling, yet when he found himself staring down the barrel at a second defeat in a week, he may have been rueing that statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LUKE POWER, SPORTS REPORTER and BEN WINSTANLEY and WILL PICKWORTH, SPORTS REPORTER and MILES STARFORTH.

Published: 15:09 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 19:33 EST, 26 November 2026.

Thomas Frank said he was happy to be 'back in the circus' at his Crystal Palace unveiling, yet when he found himself staring down the barrel at a second defeat in a week, he may have been rueing that statement.

But when Chris Richards' long-throw made its way to Jean-Philippe Mateta, everything changed on a chaotic night at Selhurst Park.

The French forward was pulled down by Jon Martin, who was sent off, and after Mateta tucked away his penalty, a flat performance and atmosphere was transformed.

Having been dominated, Palace were now quick, confident and incisive, and it was the Basque outfit who were on the ropes as Daichi Kamada saw an effort cleared off the line.

Jorgen Strand Larsen then attempted an audacious bicycle kick which fell to the feet of Dwight McNeil yards out to send the home fans into delirium.

It could have been more, but Yeremy Pino's penalty in added time was saved and Strand Larsen missed an open goal. Dean Henderson then made a brilliant stop to secure the three points.

Thomas Frank got his first win as Crystal Palace boss as his side came from behind to beat Real Sociedad 2-1.

Palace's season has been a disaster thus far, but it now has lift-off, and most importantly belief, heading into Sunday's crunch clash with Hull.

Frank, who received a warm reception from the Eagles faithful ahead of his first home game, handed rare starts to Will Hughes, Ben Chilwell and Eddie Nketiah as he rang the changes after last week’s defeat by Coventry.

They practised defending set-pieces in the warm-up in an attempt to deal with what has become their kryptonite, yet Chelsea loanee Mamadou Sarr almost turned in at the far post from a free kick just minutes in.

Can anybody stop Bournemouth? For long stretches here it looked as if their relentless march would finally be stopped - but the 10-man Cherries found another gear to continue their rampage.

In a recent development, marco Rose’s men have won 10 games in a row now, extending a club record. For two months, they have steamrolled their opponents with dauntless football and racked up an aggregate score of 25-3. They sit top of the Europa League with a perfect record.

Underneath the red and black armour, fans are starting to wonder if these players are actually of our species. Is Justin Kluivert a man or a cyborg? If you prick James Hill, does he bleed?

With each victory, the cry of the football world grows louder: somebody, please, stop this Bournemouth juggernaut, for the sake of everybody else’s trophy prospects.

Industry observers note that celta Vigo stepped up as the next challengers and thought they would be the heroes. They found Bournemouth’s net four times in all, but were denied by the offside flag for three of them. For long stretches, they were in command.

Bournemouth have now won 10 games in a row after coming from behind to beat Celta Vigo 2-1.

After a disappointing first half, Alvaro Rodriguez got them level early in the second.

Rayan scored the winner against the run of play as Bournemouth continued their perfect run in the Europa League.

In the first half, Bournemouth looked average. They were gifting away the ball in their own half, Celta found ways to sneak through their pincer-movement press, and the Spaniards had the better chances.

The first red flag came 11 minutes in, when Michele Di Gregorio spilled a save into the path of Pablo Duran, who dinked over the goalkeeper but saw his effort ruled out for offside.

Things went from bad to worse minutes later when Bafode Diakite was sent off for a stamp on Couhaib Driouech, his yellow card upgraded to a red after a review by referee Harm Osmers.

Celta almost doubled their lead when Duran beat Di Gregorio again, but he had strayed offside.

It has been revealed that but the side that emerged in the second half were unrecognisable. If Bournemouth were a man down, they played with all the swagger of having an extra body.

They were level within two minutes of the restart, Alvaro Rodriguez glancing in from Amine Adli’s header.

According to recent reports, suddenly Bournemouth were their efflorescent selves again. Antonio Silva, Adli, and Rodriguez combined for a beautiful passage of play but were spurned by the offside flag. Hill tested Ionut Radu from range.

It has been revealed that they finally got their rewards on the counter-attack, when Marcus Tavernier teed up his fellow substitute Rayan to slot past Radu and stun their hosts. Another comeback job complete.

It has been revealed that and so the Bournemouth army marches on unfettered. In the next nine days, they face Fulham, Brighton, and Hull in the Premier League. By the time they visit Arsenal in mid-December, they may be breathing down their necks.

Earlier this week, Brighton CEO Paul Barber revealed the lengths that his club go to before agreeing to sign a player.

There can be little doubt that the rigorous selection process is working, and two of their budget buys were on the scoresheet in the first half as they made light work of the Romanian champions Universitatea Craiova - and continued to make a mockery of the supposed challenge of balancing domestic and European assaults.

Brighton thrashed Romanian champions Universitatea Craiova and look capable of competing on multiple fronts.

They ended 90 minutes of domination having had 27 shots – one of which saw Femi Azeez missing the chance to make it five on debut by inexplicably blazing over from five yards.

Sunderland still have work to do if the club is to reach the Europa League’s knockout stages after Jagiellonia Bialystok held them to a 1-1 draw in a game which saw some supporters of the Polish club evade a UEFA ban and get into the Stadium of Light.

Sunderland had to settle for a 1-1 draw against Polish side Jagiellonia Bialystok.

He made six changes from the team which had held Aston Villa to a goalless draw at the weekend, again fielding a youthful team in the competition.

Industry observers note that A flat performance from a much-changed team had seen Sunderland beaten 2-0 by Croatian champions Dinamo Zagreb in their last European outing at the Stadium of Light. The big one in Europe - AC Milan at the San Siro - is next in the competition for Sunderland, with the fixture having captured the imagination of supporters.

On the pitch, it was another slow start for Le Bris’ side, though Malick Fofana tested Slawomir Abramowicz with a fine left-footed shot from outside the box.

Timur Tutierov was on target fo the Black Cats, but this was a flat performance.

It has been revealed that enzo Le Fee did well to seize on a back pass in the 30th minute and cross from the left for Nilson Angulo - who was unmarked in the box - after rounding the goalkeeper. However, his shot struck the feet of Yuki Kobayashi.

Le Bris’ team were ahead within seconds of the restart. Rigg broke through the middle, and the ball was worked to Le Fee, whose cross bounced off a visiting defender on its way to Tutierov at the far post, who headed home.

The lead did not last, with Kamil Jozwiak seizing on a Nilson Reinildo backpass before rounding Roefs to level.

Roefs denied Jozwiak at the hour-mark with a low save as home fans became increasingly frustrated with their team.

A frustrated Le Bris said: ‘It’s hard to take, because we would like to have better football, better expression.’.

A powerful HIV vaccine is finally within reach — thanks to these super antibodies

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1950 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The latest HIV-vaccine strategies aim to trigger the development of antibodies that can prevent infection by a range of HIV strains.
  • In the mid-2000s, a young woman in the KwaZulu-Natal province of South Africa became infected with HIV.
  • Although she could not control the virus without the help of drugs, the antibodies she raised against HIV are recognized as among the strongest that have ever been discovered1.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The latest HIV-vaccine strategies aim to trigger the development of antibodies that can prevent infection by a range of HIV strains. Credit: 3DMedisphere/SPL.

In the mid-2000s, a young woman in the KwaZulu-Natal province of South Africa became infected with HIV. Her story could have represented just another sobering statistic in the epidemic that was tearing through the region, but instead, she became a source of inspiration for scientists and of hope for millions. Enrolled in a study to track the course of newly acquired infections, the woman mounted a ferocious immune response to the virus over the next several years as doctors in the study treated her and took regular blood samples to monitor what was going on in her body.

Although she could not control the virus without the help of drugs, the antibodies she raised against HIV are recognized as among the strongest that have ever been discovered1. The woman is known in the literature as CAP256.

Recent findings suggest that scientists now think that by mimicking some of the key elements of an infection like hers, they might be able to train other people’s immune systems to make similarly potent antibodies that can block a diverse array of HIV strains. Ultimately, they say, they might achieve one of the most elusive goals in biomedical research: a vaccine that can stop HIV in its tracks.

The world has a golden chance to improve HIV prevention: don’t squander it.

The world has a golden chance to improve HIV prevention: don’t squander it.

According to recent reports, “We have a line of sight to an efficacious vaccine,” states Mark Feinberg, president and chief executive of the International AIDS Vaccine Initiative (IAVI) in Latest York City. “The scientific promise is greater than it’s ever been.”.

In a recent development, this year, several teams described vaccination strategies that — in monkeys — can trigger the production of what are known as broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs), molecules that can completely shut down an infection from a diverse range of HIV strains before it begins2–4. “No one has achieved that before. It’s a very important milestone,” states Rogier Sanders, a virologist at Amsterdam University Medical Centre.

Humans who have received components of similar vaccines can produce precursors to these bnAbs5–7, suggesting that with further refinement, an effective vaccine is possible.

In a recent development, success is by no means guaranteed, says Feinberg. HIV has proved a formidable foe for vaccine developers in the past. And there is another factor that adds complications. The availability of successful drugs, such as lenacapavir, that prevent HIV infection might make it difficult to test how well a vaccine works. Meanwhile, devastating cuts to the US funding that supported preclinical and clinical research for HIV have left some efforts on a precipice.

“We’re in a better position than we’ve ever been, and just at this time, we’ve seen the funding streams cut off,” says Dennis Burton, an immunologist and virologist at Scripps Research, a research institute in La Jolla, California.

The latest glimmers of success follow decades of failure. Initially, scientists looking to develop an HIV vaccine followed a strategy that had been successful for many other viruses, including hepatitis B: administer a lab-made version of the proteins that viruses use to attach to host cells and the body should start producing antibodies that will block infection. In HIV’s case, it’s the surface protein known as envelope that latches onto a molecular receptor on human T cells so that the virus can infect them. “There was only one protein, and so it seemed straightforward,” claims Sallie Permar, a vaccinologist and paediatrician at Weill Cornell Medicine in Newly introduced York City.

Starting in the 1980s, researchers made vaccines that contained the HIV envelope protein, to elicit antibodies against it, but the vaccines failed to prevent infection in clinical-trial participants. HIV mutates rapidly and most circulating strains were still able to mount an infection. “With HIV, there are millions of strains circulating simultaneously. Taking out one does nothing,” notes Richard Wyatt, a viral immunologist at Scripps Research.

Trump blew up the global fight against AIDS. Can it recover?

Trump blew up the global fight against AIDS. Can it recover?

It has been revealed that researchers tried other strategies, such as vaccines that recruited ‘killer’ T cells to wipe out infected cells, and those that delivered a wider diversity of proteins to overcome HIV’s penchant for mutation. In 2009, a clinical trial in Thailand reported modest signs of protection for a vaccine that triggered both T-cell and antibody responses8. But efforts to replicate those results failed, and that strategy was abandoned, too.

One overarching problem, indicates Feinberg, was that nobody knew what the immunological signature — the measurable biological response after injection — of an effective HIV vaccine looked like, so the only way to assess a candidate was to conduct large-scale efficacy trials and hope for the best. “It was all a shot in the dark,” says Burton.

It has been revealed that that attitude began to change after the discovery of bnAbs. In the 1990s, teams led by Burton and microbiologist Hermann Katinger, then at the University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences in Vienna, identified the first of them in individuals who were living with HIV9,10. These bnAbs could protect monkeys from infection by HIV strains circulating in Europe and America, but it took large doses, which were unlikely to be reached and sustained with a vaccine. And the protection was less effective against some strains from Africa.

In a recent development, in the 2000s, Burton’s team developed a way to sort through vast numbers of B cells — the immune cells that produce antibodies — for the rare ones that make bnAbs. After screening around 1,800 people living with HIV, they identified a pair of highly potent bnAbs, made by a donor in Africa, that blocked infection from dozens of HIV strains11. “That ignited the field,” says Burton.

Researchers would have to learn how to train the immune system to produce these kinds of bnAb. The strategies to do so emerged from the recognition that bnAbs often develop gradually in HIV-infected individuals such as CAP256. It happens through a sustained “cat and mouse game” between the fast-changing virus and an immune system struggling to keep up, claims Penny Moore, a virologist at South Africa’s National Institute for Communicable Diseases and the University of Witwatersrand, both in Johannesburg, who analysed CAP256’s blood.

In a recent development, to mimic that struggle in an uninfected person, researchers first deliver a ‘priming’ immunogen — a portion or complete copy of HIV’s envelope. This shot awakens B cells, triggering them to divide and become active. Subsequent doses deliver distinct versions of the HIV envelope to first ‘shape’ and then ‘polish’ the antibodies produced. The goal is to guide the awakened B cells through a process called affinity maturation, in which the antibodies develop extensive mutations that improve their binding and breadth. The key is that the most capable B cells are recruited early and the antibodies that they produce are honed over time (see ‘Targeted vaccines’).

Source: P. J. Klasse et al. Nature Rev. Microbiol. 23, 734–752 (2025).

It has been revealed that sanders says that this strategy, sometimes known as germline targeting, is a bit like looking for an elite footballer among pools of youth players. Rather than trying to train everyone up to an expert level, they want to identify talent early and nurture it to superstardom. “We’re scouting the talented B cells,” Sanders says.

Recent findings suggest that researchers have taken different approaches to scouting these cells. After Moore and colleagues discovered CAP256’s antibodies, they sequenced the viruses circulating in her blood to identify what might have triggered and shaped the antibodies’ production.

A modified version of the envelope protein from one such virus has shown promise as a priming agent for the immune system in monkeys and is now being trialled in humans, says virologist George Shaw who co-led the preclinical work for this2 with virologist Beatrice Hahn, both at the University of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia.

Another team, led by William Schief at Scripps Research, used computational structural modelling and cell studies to design immunogens that activate a specific subset of B cells that make antibodies capable of blocking the binding site through which HIV latches onto T cells5.

Trump team guts AIDS-eradication programme and slashes HIV research grants.

Trump team guts AIDS-eradication programme and slashes HIV research grants.

According to recent reports, in small trials of vaccination with either protein or mRNA-based versions of this immunogen12, which is called eOD-GT8, nearly all participants developed ‘bnAb precursors’. These are antibodies with the desired genetic and structural characteristics of a bnAb that blocks the T-cell binding site on the envelope protein, but not the bevy of mutations that makes bnAbs elite. In participants who also got a booster shot of a different immunogen, the antibodies picked up mutations that improved their binding and neutralization abilities. “It worked beautifully,” states Schief, who is also vice-president for protein design at Moderna Therapeutics in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that WASHINGTON, D.C.
  • Rodman jumped on Kang from behind, and the owner delighted in the surprise.
  • LITERAL GOALS.Michele Kang and Trinity Rodman celebrating the Spirit way 💃 pic.twitter.com/RpTMKhTeLd.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that WASHINGTON, D.C. – For 90 minutes, dedication to an organized plan is the default state for soccer players, but a postmatch celebration always has a randomness to it. Players and team staff scatter around a field and seem to bump into each other by coincidence, a sense of enthusiastic spontaneity coming over a wide variety of people. There was no actual shock in the fact that Trinity Rodman ran into Washington Spirit owner Michele Kang after their win over the Utah Royals in the NWSL semifinals last week. The sheer joy of reaching a third straight NWSL Championship, though, took over.

Rodman jumped on Kang from behind, and the owner delighted in the surprise. The multimillionaire, clad in a chic gray cape that embodies a dignified but serious demeanor, then wasted no time clasping her hands with Rodman's and bouncing up and down. Sports team owners are hardly ever caught so candidly; no matter how much attention they do or do not attract, they are the resident corporate types, the odd ones out next to a bunch of athletes by design. For a moment on Saturday, though, Kang and Rodman were one and the same.

LITERAL GOALS.Michele Kang and Trinity Rodman celebrating the Spirit way 💃 pic.twitter.com/RpTMKhTeLd.

It was a perfect peek inside Rodman's orbit.

Industry observers note that rodman does not lack the seriousness that Kang exudes, her commitment to her craft just as evident as her skill. She is open to any and all questions about her job, whether they are very literally about soccer or about the nature of being the NWSL's brightest star, but not ones about aliens, which she made very clear in an interaction with a content creator on Thursday. There is a non-negotiable that's just as essential to Rodman's game as her clinical instincts in front of goal, one that is crucial to her appeal -- having fun.

"I just think you shouldn't be doing anything if you're not having fun," she remarked Thursday, two days before playing in her fourth NWSL Championship with the Spirit. "I think I wouldn't be playing soccer if it wasn't fun for me, so sometimes it is hard to show it and to experience it because you are so focused and there is a lot of pressure, but I'm hoping to always be that person that allows us to let loose.".

Five years after winning the NWSL Championship at the end of a Rookie of the Year campaign, Rodman is no stranger to the league's showpiece match. The Spirit are now the finalists for a third season in a row and are still in the midst of chasing their first title since 2021, but even amid the familiarity, this year is notably different from the last. This time last year, the Spirit's headliner was battling an injury in the run-up to the final and was in the middle of negotiating what would later become a historic contract in women's soccer. She carries none of that baggage this time around.

"I'm so excited," she said. "I think going into a championship is obviously always a blessing, but going into it not 100% isn't the greatest feeling because you know that you're still going to play, but you don't know if it's going to be a great performance, so I think to be healthy and to be able to give everything that I have is really exciting for me as an individual, but also to be able to contribute to the team and get these minutes in for the last hurrah.".

According to recent reports, rodman has played 32 times this season and averaged 86.6 minutes per game along the way, an upgrade from 2025's tally of 17 matches and an average of 56.8 minutes per game during an injury-riddled campaign. It has allowed the 24-year-old to set the tone on the pitch, as well as off it.

"She's bubbly and brings energy to the changing room," defender Esme Morgan noted, speaking in the build-up to the game. "She always comes in on game day and kind of screams as she enters the changing room so you're like, 'Oh, Trin's arrived.'".

There's a playfulness to Rodman that is matched by the team as a whole, so much so that, on the drive to the team's training facility in Leesburg, Va., Morgan contemplates a list of questions that feels unique to the Spirit.

"I am excited to go in every day," Morgan mentioned. "I drive into training, and I'm looking forward to seeing the girls, and I'm thinking, 'What stupid conversation are we going to have today? What are we going to laugh about today? What silly thing are we going to do?'".

The list of silly things is endless.

It has been revealed that "We have these major red gym balls in the gym, like exercise balls, and we enjoy kind of throwing them at each other, whacking them off each other so it can get very silly," Morgan noted. "I did accidentally knock [Gabrielle] Carle off one. She was bouncing on the gym ball, and I smashed one. I was aiming for a member of staff, actually. I kicked it and then missed him slightly, bounced off the wall, hit Gabby Carle, and she fell off her exercise balls, so it was funny. She was completely fine. No Gabby Carles were harmed, but that was funny, so yeah, we've been kind of going crazy with the exercise balls.".

Then there's Jose the Coyote, a plastic good-luck charm that is emblematic of Rodman's non-negotiable.

Sources indicate that "I think just finding little things to get excited about, if it's as simple as Jose the Coyote," Rodman noted. "Just latching onto little things that we can joke around about or have fun with, but honestly, we've been having a great time. We've been growing closer, and I think even just how many fresh players we've had join the roster, I think, has almost brought us closer because we do need to have more unity and language barrier and everything forces us to be closer, so I think the close-knit group allows us to have a lot more fun because we're comfortable.".

The joy is naturally rooted in something much deeper, if equally simple, after injuries have restricted her ability to focus on the task at hand.

"I think I'm just having fun in general," she noted, "because I'm playing so that's fun for me.".

Kang's interaction with Rodman at Audi Field last weekend is the type of thing that comes up in conversation unprompted, in large part because it is a snapshot of the Spirit as a club.

Industry observers note that "Here are arguably the two people who have built us into this incredible organization with massive success," Spirit CEO Kim Stone stated. "It's because of the two of them. Trinity invests on the pitch. Michele invests in everything else ... [Rodman is] the only person who can jump up on Michele Kang and get her to dance and not get a different reaction from Michele.".

Before Rodman officially signed a deal in January worth $2 million annually, there was no question that she was worth every penny. The player is "baked into" every layer of the club's business, per Stone -- season tickets, single-game tickets, jersey sales, viewership, you name it. She is the type of player the NWSL, with much hand-wringing and a upcoming construct following a back-and-forth with the Players Association, built a whole new rule around. It is formally called the High Impact Player rule; in conversation, in headlines and on Wikipedia, it is known as the Rodman rule. A year ago, NWSL commissioner Jessica Berman used her state of the league address to say the league would "fight" to keep Rodman around as part of a larger effort to sign and retain stars. Berman took her victory lap on Thursday ahead of another glittery NWSL Championship.

"Obviously, it was incredibly notable for us to keep Trinity in this league," she stated. "The fact that she's competing in the championship again is poetic, given how far we've come and all the progress we've made. It's no secret that the next generation of fans appreciates and enjoys stars and Trinity's done an incredible job of building her celebrity off the field and we are excited that she brings that to our game. It makes people want to watch. It makes people want to follow her and her story and candidly, it's our job to continue to create more of those stories so that other people are just as excited about all of the stars that do play in the NWSL.".

Rodman, though, is singular in her value to the NWSL.

Industry observers note that "She's baked into the fact that we get asked to play Denver [Summit] in front of 60,000 people, to play Bay FC at Oracle Park, to play [in] New York for the Queens Classic," Stone noted. "If you look at all the milestone attendance, look who the opponent is. It's every time and so she's baked into all of that. I can't quantify that off the top of my head but what I can tell you is, when I worked with Miami Heat, we had LeBron James and then when I was at Golden State [Warriors], we had Steph Curry and those generational talents, what they do for your entire organization, especially when you have a good attitude and personality like Trinity, like Steph Curry, they transform your org.

It all comes down to Rodman's non-negotiable, something that will soon become a trademark as much as the goal contributions if it is not already.

"She's fun, she's engaging," Stone said. "She's what people want to be around and they're drawn to and then she's phenomenal with fans ... If you have a personality, then we can help amplify what you're trying to do. If you are vanilla ice cream, I'm going to struggle to get a lot of people interested. If you're rocky road fudge sundae with caramel pecans on top, I got something to work with. I got some unique things. I got some fun stuff to do because what people want is just the authenticity.".

It has been revealed that rodman has earned the right to be the NWSL's transformational, singular talent, successfully receiving a torch that was left behind a few years ago by members of the 2019 Women's World Cup-winning U.S. team that captivated a nation.

It has been revealed that "Trin is a generational talent," Stone said. "She transcends soccer. She is arguably the face of soccer in America, men's or women's, hard stop ... What you end up with is the most popular player in our league, the most sold jerseys in our league. The people used to shout for Alex Morgan. Now they're all shouting for Trinity.".
